explanation_record.author: Tristen Pierson
explanation_record.explanation_text: The program checked this claim against three pieces of evidence, and all three point the other way. First, published work by other researchers (Rao and colleagues, 2009) measured how predictable each sign is from the signs before it - a measure called conditional entropy. The Indus values fell inside the range seen for real language writing, and outside the range seen for non-linguistic symbol sets. Second, the program's own positional battery (Phase-43) found 20 signs that behave like word endings - they sit at the end of texts the way suffixes do. Third, the same battery found a fixed two-sign formula that opens inscriptions, the way a title or heading does. Non-linguistic emblem sets are not expected to show grammar-like habits of either kind. The claim also carries its own test on the record - it would be in trouble if the entropy data fell in the linguistic range and positional patterns rose above a random baseline - and that is the result the checks returned. On the strength of this, the program records the claim as contradicted. One caution belongs in the open: two of the three contradicting items come from the program's own test battery, run on corpora from one lineage (the Mahadevan/ICIT line). The published entropy result is the only one of the three that was produced entirely outside this program.

falsifier: Conditional entropy data in linguistic range; positional pattern above random baseline.

explanation_record.author: Tristen Pierson
explanation_record.explanation_text: The support on the record comes from two comparisons the program ran in its Phase-41 and Phase-43 work. Both asked the same question: if you anchor a small set of signs to Dravidian word values, do the resulting sign sequences look more probable than the same exercise done with Sanskrit values? In the first run (Phase-41, on the Mahadevan corpus of 1,669 inscriptions, five anchor signs per language), the Dravidian anchors won by a ratio of 1.0566 to 1 - a real but small margin. In the second (Phase-43, on a 1,500-sequence sample of the V3 corpus), Dravidian won by 0.484 log units per sign - again a win, again modest. That is why the status is partially supported rather than supported: the comparisons favour Dravidian over Sanskrit, but only two candidate families were compared, and the margins are small. The weakness that matters most must be stated in the open: both comparisons were computed with the program's semantic-anchoring machinery, and the program later falsified that method on held-out data (Phase-107: its predictions scored 0.000, 0 of 115). No rerun of this specific Dravidian-versus-Sanskrit comparison with a method that survived testing exists in the record. The partial support on this claim is therefore inherited from a method the program no longer trusts, and the claim's checked status has never been re-earned without it.

falsifier: If Dravidian phonotactics do not fit Indus sign bigrams better than Sanskrit.
statement: Indus script encodes Proto-Dravidian language using the rebus principle.

explanation_record.author: Tristen Pierson
explanation_record.explanation_text: The program's check (Phase-43, test T2.4) asked whether the signs that follow the fish sign behave the way case endings (suffixes) should if the fish sign were a word being read aloud. For Mahadevan sign 72, the answer was yes: in 181 occurrences, the sign that follows it is a text-ending sign 25.9 percent of the time, matching the pattern the test required, and the test marked it supported. But the same test tried six fish candidates, and the family's most frequent member, sign 267 (356 occurrences), failed clearly: its followers end the text only 3.8 percent of the time. The claim as written - the fish sign, as a family, is the primary rebus sign - is therefore only partly supported: one member behaves as the reading predicts, the commonest member does not. A further caution: which drawn sign counts as 'the fish sign' is itself not fully settled across the field's compilations - the program's own cross-compilation study (Phase-125) found the two great sign lists disagree far more than they agree, so a reading tied to one list's numbering carries that uncertainty with it.

explanation_record.author: Tristen Pierson
explanation_record.explanation_text: The program tested the shape of this claim, and the shape held up. In the test recorded on the claim (the positional test in the program's analysis files), 805 of 2,267 inscriptions of three or more signs followed the opening-middle-ending structure - 35.5 percent, against 0.6 percent expected by chance, a lift of about 59 times. The test also found the position-strong signs the pattern needs: 40 signs that strongly prefer the opening, 20 that strongly prefer the ending, and 61 for the middle. That is why the status is partially supported. The limit of the support is written in the test's own verdict, and it should be quoted rather than softened: the pattern is 'consistent with both Hunt model and Dravidian suffix model. Cannot distinguish between them without visual sign classification.' In other words, the check shows a three-part positional pattern exists. It does not show that the parts carry the meanings Hunt assigns them, and the same pattern is equally consistent with a rival account in which the closing signs are simply word endings in a language.

author: Tristen Pierson
does_not_establish: A Zipf-style curve is weak evidence about meaning. Many systems that are not language at all - and some random processes - produce similar curves, so the fit cannot distinguish writing from non-writing, let alone identify a language. The exponent's exact value also moves with corpus size and with how signs are split or merged, and the field's compilations disagree on the sign inventory itself. What this claim does not establish: that the script encodes language, that any sign has any value, or that the corpus the curve was fitted on is complete. What would strengthen it: the same fit on an independent corpus with a sign inventory fixed in advance, reported alongside the fits for known non-linguistic symbol systems.

explanation_record.explanation_text: The program reran this check on its V3 corpus in Phase-43 and the fit held: the recorded exponent is about 1.35, in the range the original work reported. The claim carries a proper falsifier - it fails if the frequency distribution departs from the Zipf-Mandelbrot law - and the distribution did not depart. That is the whole of the support, and it is genuine as far as it goes. Two record-keeping cautions belong with it. First, the same claim was extracted twice (from Yadav's 2009 paper and the 2010 follow-up), and for a time the program's claim set counted this one test result twice, on two records; the Phase I dedupe of 2026-10-12 merged them into this single claim, keeping the 2010 record as an evidence instance rather than a second claim. Second, the check was run by the program itself, on a corpus from the same Mahadevan lineage the original study used.

statement: The PRED-2026 register is untouched by Spec 028.

does_not_establish: Governed Indus claims: extracted literature claims and anchor-reading claims, in the AEE wiring (aee_core), the claims API, and every display surface.
falsifier: A governed claim representation (API response, stored record, or rendered surface) that carries a score or verdict but no lifecycle stage defeats this claim.
A lifecycle stage value outside the five-value set in any governed artifact defeats this claim.
statement: Every governed Indus claim carries a lifecycle stage drawn from the fixed five-value stage set.

does_not_establish: All stage transitions in the AEE wiring, the research loop, intake, and any batch or scheduled process.
falsifier: A stage-transition log entry advancing a claim past checked whose actor is a process, job, model, or pipeline defeats this claim.
statement: Transitions past the checked stage take effect only through a recorded act of a named human.

does_not_establish: Anchor readings (the 287-anchor set and successors) and any future headline decipherment claim. Literature claims are governed by C01 but are not required to be bundles.
falsifier: An anchor reading displayed or stored as a single-stage, single-score object with no sub-claim records defeats this claim.
statement: Each anchor reading is a bundle of four named sub-claims with individual stages.

does_not_establish: The accepted and digested transitions for every governed claim.
falsifier: A claim at accepted with no explanation record naming a human author defeats this claim.
statement: Acceptance of a claim requires a filed explanation record authored by a named human.

does_not_establish: Decipherment claims (anchor-reading bundles per C03); the cap binds stage, not score or verdict.
falsifier: A decipherment claim whose attribution sub-claim is contested while its displayed parent stage exceeds the adjudicated cap defeats this claim.
A decipherment claim with no attribution sub-claim record defeats this claim.
statement: Attribution is a registered sub-claim of every decipherment claim.

does_not_establish: Frontend surfaces, API summary responses, generated reports, exports, and public pages produced by the program.
falsifier: A surface whose headline or summary position carries a score, band, mean, or count as the claim's standing defeats this claim (the current 'N signs deciphered' headline is a standing counterexample this spec exists to remove).
statement: Scores appear on program surfaces only inside checking-stage evidence presentations.

does_not_establish: Claims API responses and every frontend/report rendering of claim standing.
falsifier: A rendering in which an AEE band, score, or extraction status occupies the visual position or vocabulary reserved for scholarly acceptance defeats this claim.
statement: Lane-1 state is stored apart from lane-2 state on every governed claim.

does_not_establish: Readings submitted by scholars outside the program. Program-internal predictions remain governed by docs/PREDICTION_REGISTER.md.
falsifier: A registration workflow that requires a program verdict, score, or stage before a timestamp is issued defeats this claim.
A registered reading whose credit display changes when the program's assessment of it changes defeats this claim.
statement: An external reading registered at intake receives a priority timestamp independent of program assessment.

does_not_establish: Verdicts and stage transitions recorded after this spec is implemented; historical records are addressed only as OD-1 decides.
falsifier: A verdict or stage transition whose claim-level API representation lacks any one of: evidence refs, origin groups, falsifier state, actor, timestamp — defeats this claim.
statement: Every decision record on a governed claim carries an inspectable evidence trail inside the claim API representation.

does_not_establish: Spec 029 and all work done under it before an adjudicated, frozen implementation plan exists.
falsifier: A diff under this spec that alters an existing claim record, anchor record, verdict, or display string defeats this claim.
statement: This claims-first draft leaves every existing record exactly as published.

does_not_establish: Anchor readings (the 287-anchor set and successors) and any future headline decipherment claim. Literature claims are governed by C01 but are not required to be bundles.
falsifier: A parent stage higher than any one of its sub-claim stages defeats this claim.
statement: The stage of an anchor reading equals the minimum stage among its sub-claims.

does_not_establish: The accepted and digested transitions for every governed claim.
falsifier: A claim at digested with no digestion record defeats this claim.
statement: Digestion of a claim requires a filed digestion record evidencing independent scholarly engagement.

does_not_establish: Frontend surfaces, API summary responses, generated reports, exports, and public pages produced by the program.
falsifier: A verdict display with no not-understood statement defeats this claim.
statement: Every verdict display carries an explicit statement of remaining unknowns.

does_not_establish: The assessment rule set for Q6 timing-support. This claim governs the criteria, not the spine data (C02/C03) and not the conduct of the re-test (C05). The frozen set comprises the four thresholds of stage0-freeze.md section 4 with the 5250-3850 BP window and the Stage 0 grade and material vocabularies; the extension changes none of them.
falsifier: A re-test run under any threshold, window, grade rule, or material mapping differing from stage0-freeze.md section 4 and section 3.3 defeats this claim.
statement: The Q6 timing-support criteria applied to the extended spine are exactly the criteria frozen in Spec 027 Stage 0 freeze.

does_not_establish: Row-level provenance of extension-built chronology rows. Grading and material rules themselves are inherited from the Stage 0 freeze; this claim governs traceability, not grading outcomes. The trace fields are origin source, source locator, lab code, licence state, origin group, region as recorded, and scenario tag where applicable; a row missing any trace field is not built.
falsifier: One built extension row lacking any named trace field defeats this claim.
statement: Every chronology row the extension builds carries the complete trace the Stage 0 freeze requires.

does_not_establish: Counting identity of measurements across the extension's overlapping routes (R5/R1/R2/R3). This claim does not govern site clustering, which follows the Stage 0 name normalisation. Measurement identity is the lab code, corroborated by age and material, across XRONOS, origin databases, aggregators, and literature extraction; the assessment pool inherits the same identity rule.
falsifier: Two rows in the assessment pool sharing a lab code with matching age and material, counted as independent measurements, defeat this claim.
statement: No radiocarbon measurement is counted more than once within the extended spine.

does_not_establish: Reporting of the re-test and of any later Q6 support assessment using the extended spine. This claim does not itself decide whether the sensitivity binds a future Q6 freeze; that is Ask 2 for owner adjudication. Dependence on contested chronology is the claim's subject: the as-frozen computation includes CONTESTED-scenario rows, the sensitivity computation excludes them, and both are published side by side.
falsifier: A re-test report lacking the with/without-CONTESTED line for any criterion defeats this claim.
statement: The re-test reports every criterion under both computations: the full pool plus the pool minus CONTESTED-scenario rows.

does_not_establish: Conduct of the extension's re-test. The future Q6 freeze's own model decisions (Bayesian model, priors, rival thresholds under Spec 027 section 8.2) are outside this claim and outside this spec. No trait list is built, no first-appearance outcome is examined, and no timing model is fitted before or during the timing-support assessment.
falsifier: Any trait-timing output, trait list, or fitted timing model among the extension's products defeats this claim.
statement: The re-test inspects spine margins together with metadata only.

does_not_establish: Use and publication of extension data. Internal-spine use of open_access_read_only rows follows the Phase-124 precedent; this claim governs posture and release, not row admission (C02). No open_access_read_only or catalogue_only material enters any CC BY release package.
falsifier: One open_access_read_only or catalogue_only row in a release manifest defeats this claim.
statement: Licence posture follows Spec 027 section 5.1 for every extension row.

does_not_establish: Closure semantics of the extension study. This claim governs responses to a negative result; it does not prejudge whether the result will be negative. On a negative outcome Q6 stays NOT-YET-TESTABLE; the outcome is never grounds to loosen a criterion, re-grade by inference, or substitute period labels for dates.
falsifier: Any criterion loosened, grade inferred, or period-label timing table offered as a substitute following a negative extension outcome defeats this claim.
statement: A negative extension outcome is a valid closure of the extension study.

does_not_establish: The licensed-conclusion boundary of every Q7 output. Craft evidence means objects, materials, and techniques, and nothing beyond them. This claim governs what a verdict may mean, not how links are built (C02-C04), not how arms are computed (C05-C07), and not how verdicts are issued (C09).
falsifier: One people, migration, workshop-population, or language conclusion in a Q7 report defeats this claim.
statement: Q7 verdicts under Spec 031 concern craft evidence only.

does_not_establish: Membership of the primary link set. This claim governs which determinations may enter the primary tier, not the sensitivity tier (C03), not contextual sources (C04), and not release (C11).
falsifier: One reference-based or method-unrecorded determination in the primary link set defeats this claim.
statement: The primary link set contains only Law (2011) determinations made by a named instrumental method.

does_not_establish: Placement of Law's Chapter 4 reference-based assignments. This claim governs labelling and placement, not primary membership (C02) and not arm closure (C08).
falsifier: One reference-based assignment inside the primary link set, or one sensitivity result reported without its label, defeats this claim.
statement: Reference-based assignments from Law (2011) enter only the separately labelled sensitivity tier.

does_not_establish: The role of the Possehl (1996) Meluhha compilation. This claim governs link contribution only; the compilation's contextual use in narrative is outside every link set, covariate, and sensitivity.
falsifier: One site-pair link, covariate value, or sensitivity cell derived from the Meluhha compilation defeats this claim.
statement: The Meluhha compilations contribute no site-pair links under this design.

does_not_establish: Arm separation in computation. This claim governs the site sets and the ban on pooling the arms into one score; it does not govern either arm's response basis (C06 for bead/craft; spec section 4.2 for ceramic) or arm closure (C07, C08).
falsifier: One pooled cross-arm score, or one arm computed on the other arm's site set, defeats this claim.
statement: The two response arms are computed on separate eligible site sets.

does_not_establish: The bead/craft arm's response basis. The classifications reach assemblages through their published applications; a cell's value is taken from a published application of the classification, with that application recorded as the cell's source. This claim governs source basis and per-cell source recording, not the arm's site set (C05) and not link construction (C02, C03).
falsifier: One bead/craft response cell built from a program-generated classification, or lacking its published classification source, defeats this claim.
statement: The bead/craft response is built only from published Kenoyer/Vidale technique classifications.

does_not_establish: The ceramic arm's estimability at the margins step. This claim governs the ceramic arm's closure consequence only; the general viability rule for both arms is C08, and the thresholds' provenance is C12.
falsifier: One ceramic response computed after a margins step that evidenced fewer than the frozen minimum eligible sites defeats this claim.
statement: The ceramic arm is NOT ESTIMABLE under this freeze if the execution margins step cannot evidence the frozen minimum eligible site count from sources at audited postures.

does_not_establish: Arm closure on viability. This claim governs the consequence of unmet thresholds (8 eligible sites, 10 linked pairs) for either arm; it does not set the thresholds (C12) and does not govern the ceramic source-basis closure (C07).
falsifier: One primary test run for an arm that failed the frozen viability thresholds at the margins step defeats this claim.
statement: An arm failing the frozen viability thresholds at the margins step closes NOT-YET-TESTABLE.

does_not_establish: Verdict issuance discipline for both arms, including the controls and the site jackknife. This claim governs how verdicts are produced, not what they may mean (C01) and not arm eligibility (C05, C08).
falsifier: One verdict issued after a failed control, or one SUPPORTED verdict whose effect depends on a single site under the frozen jackknife, defeats this claim.
statement: A Q7 verdict is issued only under the frozen verdict rules.

does_not_establish: The period-eligibility control. This claim governs the eligibility input only; it asserts no timing result, and sub-period-resolution variants are outside this design entirely.
falsifier: One site pair admitted on a period assignment finer than the published gazetteer labels, or one sub-period variant tested under this design, defeats this claim.
statement: Period eligibility for site pairs rests only on Stage 0 gazetteer period labels as published.

does_not_establish: Release posture of derived data. This claim governs publication of derived link and response data; the registration half of adopted Ask 6A (OSF registration of the frozen contract before execution) is recorded in the spec and freeze record and is not part of this claim's text.
falsifier: One released row derived from an open_access_read_only source defeats this claim.
statement: No released row is derived from an open_access_read_only source.

does_not_establish: The provenance of the support thresholds (DD-1, DD-2, DD-3): their values come from the D8 audit margins and they were fixed in this freeze, before any response was computed. This claim governs where the thresholds come from and when they were fixed; the consequences of unmet thresholds are C07 and C08.
falsifier: One support threshold in this design that was set or changed after any response was computed, or that cites a margin the D8 audit does not report, defeats this claim.
statement: Support thresholds take their values from the D8 audit margins.

does_not_establish: The licensed-conclusion boundary of every Spec 032 output. This claim governs what a verdict may mean. It does not govern how the trained set is built (C03), how the score is computed (C08), or how the outcome is recorded (C11). The verdict states the criterion outcome and nothing beyond that statement.
falsifier: One conclusion in a Spec 032 report that reads beyond the registered statement (a meaning, a mechanism, or another site) defeats this claim.
statement: Spec 032 verdicts state whether the registered PRED-2026-006 criterion is met on the withheld Harappa data.

does_not_establish: The criterion claim. It fixes the two registered numbers (the 70 percent share; the 0.40 start-rate bar) exactly as registered on 2026-04-22. It does not fix how the trained set is obtained (C03), how signs map (C06), or how the share is computed (C08).
falsifier: One Spec 032 scoring that applies a threshold, a band, or an adjustment other than the registered pair (70 percent; 0.40) defeats this claim.
statement: The registered success criterion is a share of at least 70 percent of the frozen trained INITIAL signs with a Harappa start rate of at least 0.40.

does_not_establish: The trained-set provenance claim. It governs where the sign set comes from (the recorded lineage of the global class stability check) and when it is fixed (before counting). It does not govern the closure that follows if reconstruction fails (C04) or the crosswalk that maps the set (C06).
falsifier: One scoring under Spec 032 whose sign set was built fresh, sampled, or altered after counting began defeats this claim.
statement: The trained INITIAL sign set is the set reconstructed from the recorded CISI Mohenjo-daro training lineage.

does_not_establish: The trained-set closure claim. It governs the single stated consequence of a step-0.1 failure. It does not govern the withholding closure (C05 carries the parallel rule for step 0.2) or the reporting of closures (C12).
falsifier: One run under Spec 032 that proceeds to a verdict after the trained set failed to reproduce defeats this claim.
statement: The study closes as CANNOT BE RUN AS WRITTEN when step 0.1 fails.

does_not_establish: The withholding claim. It states the fact step 0.2 verifies: the training lineage is CISI Mohenjo-daro only. It records the corpus's prior unrelated exposure (Phases 281-293) as context to be stated openly at execution; exposure alone neither proves nor defeats the withholding. It does not govern the trained set's reconstruction (C03).
falsifier: One record showing Harappa Yajnadevam sequences inside the INITIAL training lineage defeats this claim.
statement: The INITIAL class assignments derive from CISI Mohenjo-daro training only.

does_not_establish: The sign-identity claim. It governs the mapping instrument (the existing published crosswalk files) and its fixing time (before counting). It does not govern the trained set itself (C03) or the treatment of signs the mapping cannot carry (C07).
falsifier: One scored sign whose identity was assigned outside the frozen crosswalk files defeats this claim.
statement: Sign identity under Spec 032 is built only from the existing crosswalk files.

does_not_establish: The coverage claim. It governs the residue of the mapping (C06): its counting, its label, and the first-sentence rule above 20 percent. It does not change the criterion (C02) or the denominator rule of the computation (C08 states the share over the trained set with this coverage stated).
falsifier: One Spec 032 outcome that omits the unmappable count, or that buries above-20-percent coverage below the first sentence, defeats this claim.
statement: Unmappable coverage above 20 percent of the trained set is stated in the verdict's first sentence.

does_not_establish: The computation claim. It fixes the scored quantity (the share), its population (the frozen trained set of C03, mapped under C06), and its data (the withheld Harappa sequences only). It does not fix the bar the share is judged against (C02) or the descriptive table published with it (C09).
falsifier: One Spec 032 score computed on any data beyond the withheld Harappa sequences, or with any adjustment the registration does not state, defeats this claim.
statement: The score is the share of frozen trained INITIAL signs with a Harappa start rate of at least 0.40 on the withheld Harappa sequences.

does_not_establish: The descriptive-record claim. It governs the one pre-registered addition to the registered computation: the per-sign table. The table is descriptive only. It does not govern the score (C08) or the verdict (C02), and no reading of the table moves either. The table lists every trained sign, its Harappa count, and its start rate.
falsifier: One Spec 032 outcome missing the per-sign table, or one verdict argued from the table against the share, defeats this claim.
An outcome under this spec published without the per-sign table defeats this claim.
statement: The per-sign table is published with the outcome as a descriptive record.

does_not_establish: The independence-wording claim. It bounds the independence language of the verdict to site-withholding (Harappa held out of training, C05). It does not restate the conclusion boundary (C01): C01 bounds what the verdict is about; C10 bounds the independence it may claim. Scholarly-lineage independence is not claimed, because the Yajnadevam compilation's object base is published-corpus material.
falsifier: One Spec 032 verdict statement claiming lineage independence, or omitting the within-lineage limit, defeats this claim.
Any Spec 035 outcome statement claiming lineage independence, or omitting the small-set caveat from its first paragraph, defeats this claim.
statement: The verdict wording claims only the site-withholding independence the registration specified.

does_not_establish: The register-handling claim. It governs how the outcome enters the program record (append-only, dated, at execution). It does not govern the verdict itself (C02) and it performs no register change at this freeze: the freeze leaves every register byte as it stands. The register's existing text stays byte-identical.
falsifier: One edited (not appended) register byte attributable to Spec 032 defeats this claim.
statement: The outcome is appended to the PRED register as a dated entry at execution.

does_not_establish: The closure-reporting claim. It governs the wording of the two soft landings the design allows. It does not govern when a closure triggers (C04 for the trained set; C05's verification for the withholding) or the verdict mapping that applies when no closure triggers (C02). The closures are CANNOT BE RUN AS WRITTEN and the UNMAPPABLE coverage statement.
falsifier: One Spec 032 closure reported in verdict vocabulary defeats this claim.
statement: Step-0 closures are reported in closure vocabulary only.

does_not_establish: The licensed-conclusion boundary of every Spec 033 output. The bounded comparison is: which family's published word-values, assigned to the frozen anchor signs, make the inscription sequences most probable under the frozen counted model. A verdict under this spec is not evidence for the rebus method, not a reading of any single sign, and not a decipherment. This claim governs what a verdict may mean; it does not govern the pipeline (C03, C08), the data (C04, C05), or the criteria (C10-C12).
falsifier: One conclusion in a Spec 033 report that reads a fit result as the rebus method, a sign reading, or a decipherment defeats this claim.
statement: Spec 033 verdicts concern the bounded language comparison only.

does_not_establish: The hypothesis claim, stated as the design states it. The margin the hypothesis must clear is fixed by C10; the range condition is fixed by C11; this claim states the ordering the run tests. It does not fix the estimator (C08), the anchor set (C06), or the values (C07). The named rivals are Indo-Aryan (Sanskrit), Munda, and the no-language (isolate-baseline) assignments.
falsifier: One primary run under the frozen pipeline in which the best rival matches or beats Dravidian, or random assignments reach Dravidian's range, defeats this claim (the design's falsifier).
statement: Proto-Dravidian assignments produce inscription sequences with higher probability than every named rival under the frozen counted model.

does_not_establish: The method-purity claim (H26). It bars the falsified SA machinery and every SA-derived quantity from every part of the run: family scoring, controls, robustness arm, and sensitivity. It does not govern what the pipeline contains instead (C08 states the counted model). Anchor promotion is barred on the same terms: no anchor is promoted, and no promoted value enters any score.
falsifier: One SA computation, anchor promotion, or SA-derived input anywhere in a Spec 033 run defeats this claim.
statement: Spec 033 runs without semantic anchoring.

does_not_establish: The sign-set claim. The strict sign set is the 94 readings carrying validation status strict_sa_independent in backend/reports/INDUS_FINAL_ANCHORS.json (287 anchors in total). It does not govern the corpus the sequences come from (C05) or the anchors chosen inside the set (C06).
falsifier: One scored sequence under Spec 033 containing a reading outside the strict set defeats this claim.
statement: Spec 033 scoring uses the strict sign set only.

does_not_establish: The corpus claim. The corpus family is the one the original Phase-41/43 comparisons used, so the rerun is comparable to them. The within-lineage limit this choice carries is governed by C14, not hidden by this claim. It does not govern the sign set scored over the corpus (C04).
falsifier: One Spec 033 score computed on a corpus other than the held V3/Mahadevan-lineage corpus defeats this claim.
statement: The scored corpus is the program's V3/Mahadevan-lineage corpus as held in the database.

does_not_establish: The anchor-set claim. The set follows the five-per-language pattern of the original Phase-41 comparison and is frozen as cited data before any family is scored. It does not govern the values assigned to the signs (C07) or the second anchor list of the robustness arm (C13).
falsifier: One family scored under Spec 033 on an anchor set other than the frozen five-sign set defeats this claim.
statement: Each family's anchor signs are the same frozen five-sign set.

does_not_establish: The values-provenance claim. The published sources are: the Dravidian Etymological Dictionary tradition for Dravidian; standard Sanskrit lexicon values for Indo-Aryan; published Munda reconstructions for Munda. It does not govern which signs carry values (C06, C13) or how values enter the score (C08).
falsifier: One anchor value under Spec 033 without a named published source defeats this claim.
statement: Anchor values come from published sources only.

does_not_establish: The estimator claim. The pipeline is the estimator fixed at this freeze (spec section 5): counted conditional probabilities over phoneme-sequence and sign-identity units, estimated from the corpus itself under each mapping, add-one smoothing, mean log probability per sign. It does not govern the anchor set or values the pipeline consumes (C06, C07) or the controls it must also score (C09 names them).
falsifier: One family or control scored under Spec 033 by a pipeline differing in estimator, smoothing, or scoring rule defeats this claim.
statement: All scoring under Spec 033 uses the identical counted-model pipeline.

does_not_establish: The controls claim. The random assignments permute the same values over the same anchor signs, giving the no-information distribution the verdict rules use (C10, C11). The no-language baseline carries no values on the anchor signs. It does not govern the verdict thresholds applied to the control distribution (C10, C11). The second control, the no-language baseline, also runs in the same pass.
falsifier: One Spec 033 verdict issued without the 999-assignment distribution and the baseline from the same pass defeats this claim.
statement: The no-information control distribution is 999 random assignments run in the same pass as the families.

does_not_establish: The SUPPORTED-rule claim (margin condition). The bar is the design's, set from the original margins (Phase-41: 1.0566 to 1; Phase-43: 0.484 log units per sign) so the rerun can fail the claim. The best rival is the highest-scoring of the Sanskrit, Munda, and no-language baseline assignments on the primary run. The rule's second condition (the random-distribution percentile) is C15's claim. It does not govern the other verdicts (C11, C12).
falsifier: One SUPPORTED verdict under Spec 033 issued below either condition defeats this claim.
statement: The SUPPORTED margin is at least 0.10 log units per sign over the highest-scoring rival assignment.

does_not_establish: The NOT SUPPORTED-rule claim (rival trigger). Its second trigger, stated here in full: Dravidian inside the random distribution's range also yields NOT SUPPORTED; either trigger suffices. The status consequence of a NOT SUPPORTED outcome (the inherited partial support replaced by an appended, dated entry; the old SA-based numbers kept in history, labelled) is governed by spec section 6. It does not govern the SUPPORTED rules (C10, C15) or the sub-margin case (C12).
falsifier: One run meeting either trigger whose outcome is recorded as anything other than NOT SUPPORTED defeats this claim.
statement: Dravidian failing to finish strictly first yields NOT SUPPORTED.

does_not_establish: The INCONCLUSIVE-rule claim. The Harappa-removed comparison is a pre-registered sensitivity: it is reported in full, the verdict rests on the primary run, and a ranking reversal there is this rule's second trigger. It does not govern the primary-run rules (C10, C11).
falsifier: One run meeting either trigger whose outcome is recorded as SUPPORTED or NOT SUPPORTED defeats this claim.
statement: A winning margin below 0.10 log units per sign yields INCONCLUSIVE.

does_not_establish: The robustness-arm claim. The second list is the next five published candidates per family, frozen as cited data with the primary list before any scoring. The arm is reported with the outcome; the verdict rules of C10-C12 read the primary list's run. It does not govern the primary anchor set (C06).
falsifier: One Spec 033 outcome missing the robustness arm, or one verdict argued from the arm against the primary run, defeats this claim.
statement: The second pre-registered anchor list is run as a robustness arm under the identical pipeline.

does_not_establish: The lineage-wording claim. A win under this spec is a win inside the Mahadevan lineage: the corpora of both the original comparisons and this rerun are Mahadevan-lineage, and no independent-corpus replication exists in the record. Designs D-01 and D-24 are the ones that speak to other lineages. It does not restate the conclusion boundary (C01): C01 bounds what the verdict is about; C14 bounds the independence it may claim.
falsifier: One Spec 033 verdict statement claiming cross-lineage independence, or omitting the lineage limit, defeats this claim.
statement: Spec 033 verdict wording names the within-lineage limit.

does_not_establish: The SUPPORTED-rule claim (percentile condition). The distribution is the 999 random assignments of C09, run under the identical pipeline in the same pass. The condition is the design's, fixed alongside the margin of C10 from the original results. It does not govern the margin condition (C10) or the other verdicts (C11, C12). The bar is applied to Dravidian's primary-run score: SUPPORTED requires that score above this percentile.
falsifier: One SUPPORTED verdict under Spec 033 issued with Dravidian at or below the 99th percentile of the random-assignment distribution defeats this claim.
statement: The SUPPORTED percentile bar is the 99th percentile of the random-assignment distribution.

does_not_establish: Scope claim for the whole spec. The settled result (STUDY-SPEC-019/PHASE-125: FAIL - DISAGREEMENT) is the input, not a question; the attribution outcome, whichever way it falls, is a statement about the residue's composition. It does not govern the bridge (C03), the gate (C04), or the verdict lines (C09-C11). Which compilation is right is never judged under this spec.
falsifier: Any Spec 034 outcome statement naming a compilation as correct, or re-opening the Phase-125 verdict, defeats this claim.
statement: Spec 034 attributes the Phase-125 disagreement residue only.

does_not_establish: The hypothesis claim (design D-20). 'Far better' is made exact by the frozen verdict lines of C09-C11 on the matched-object median distance against the corpus-level 0.637 (Phase-125 median TV 0.636931). It does not govern the step-0 gate (C04-C05), which decides whether this hypothesis is reached at all.
falsifier: A matched-object median distance at or above 0.32 (C10's line) falsifies this claim, as designed.
statement: Matched-object positional profiles agree far better than the corpus-level profiles.

does_not_establish: Bridge-construction claim. Every bridge pair enters as cited data with its source: route (a) the 7,705-row CISI catalogue of Phases 120-124; route (b) Mahadevan-side published object references through the Phase-130 intake schema; route (c) the 44 Phase-128 dossiers. No other route is used. It does not govern the gate count (C04) or the prohibited join (C06).
falsifier: One bridge pair in the Spec 034 census sourced outside routes (a)-(c), or entered without a cited source, defeats this claim.
statement: Step 0 builds the object bridge through three named routes.

does_not_establish: Gate claim (design D-20, fixed in advance). A matched object counts only if its text, in each compilation, has three or more signs. The gate is applied to the bridge census of C03 before any measurement. It does not govern the below-gate closure (C05) or the measurement rules (C07).
falsifier: Any step-1 measurement under Spec 034 on a bridge census below 150 qualifying objects defeats this claim.
statement: The step-0 gate is 150 matched objects.

does_not_establish: Below-gate closure claim (design D-20), governed by spec section 4. No attribution verdict is issued below the gate. It does not govern the gate itself (C04) or the step-1 verdict lines (C09-C11).
falsifier: Any attribution verdict under Spec 034 issued on a bridge census below the gate defeats this claim.
statement: The below-gate closure is TOO THIN TO ATTRIBUTE.

does_not_establish: Prohibited-join claim. Phase-131 established that Holdat cisi_number is internal sequential numbering, not a CISI object ID, and rejected that join (179 apparent namesakes, 0 validated); the prohibition is carried here unchanged. It does not govern the admitted routes (C03).
falsifier: One bridge pair under Spec 034 joined on Holdat cisi_number defeats this claim.
statement: Holdat cisi_number is a prohibited join key under Spec 034.

does_not_establish: Method claim. falsifier: Any join computed in a run whose step 0 did not first record all five verifications passing defeats this claim.
statement: Execution step 0 precedes any join computation, fail-closed.

does_not_establish: Coverage and attribution. A sampled pilot would leave the spine's coverage undefined for the unexamined remainder (DD-037-2). The stratum samples across all three outcome classes (its size is the freeze proposal DD-037-5) and reports class-split counts as aggregates; it re-grades nothing and repairs nothing (C04) - a conflict attributed to extraction error remains a conflict in the pilot's counts, with the attribution reported beside them. The grading is a census, not a sample (DD-037-2). The seeded hand-check stratum exists to attribute conflicts to causes - intake extraction error, programme-side record error, genuine compilation divergence, or true non-identity.
falsifier: Any candidate left ungraded in a completed pilot, or any conflict rate reported without the stratum's cause attribution beside it, defeats this claim.
statement: Under Spec 037, the pilot grades the 693 candidates.

does_not_establish: Reporting discipline. No other quantities are computed for publication, and no reported share silently changes its base: outcome shares are over the full 693-candidate census, field-specific bases are named where a field could not grade every candidate. Merging UNRESOLVED into VERIFIED (or dropping it from a denominator) is the specific rounding-up this claim exists to forbid. The aggregates are outcome counts and shares overall, by portion section, and by corpus source, with conflict reason breakdowns and per-field graded bases; UNRESOLVED is always reported as its own class.
falsifier: Any Spec 037 report whose classes do not sum to the census, or that folds UNRESOLVED into another class, defeats this claim.
statement: Under Spec 037, the reported quantities are the pre-registered aggregates of spec section 4.4.

does_not_establish: Workstream B's character. Bracketed period codes are typological ascriptions by the volume and are reported separately from unbracketed codes; mixed codes (1/2, M, S) are their own classes; no code is re-derived or corrected under this study. The annex's numbers come from the pinned local table, recomputed at execution and reported as found against the intake's census (1,094 HARP records; lot fill 754; period fill 656, a floor). It reports dig-year, lot, and period-code inventories and distributions as printed, with the period-fill rate always carrying its floor caveat (the scan's text layer loses split period tokens, so the fill is a floor, not the printed rate).
falsifier: Any annex statement interpreting the distributions as chronological findings, or any period-fill figure printed without its floor caveat, defeats this claim.
statement: The HARP annex is descriptive only.

does_not_establish: The non-reopening fence. Q7's closure turned on cross-site link mass among eligible sites; Harappa-internal provenance structure is not a link between sites, so nothing in the annex bears on the margins step that closed Q7. A future study that would use this structure as evidence requires its own spec, freeze, and - where it touches Q7 - a reopening decision recorded as such; this spec is not that study. The Q7 finding stands as recorded - in-universe link mass 2 sites / 1 pair, bead/craft arm NOT-YET-TESTABLE, ceramic arm NOT ESTIMABLE - and no quantity in the annex feeds a verdict without its own frozen study.
falsifier: Any Spec 037 product recording a Q7 status change, or supplying a quantity to another study's verdict without that study's own freeze, defeats this claim.
statement: The HARP annex does not change the Spec 031 (Q7) finding.

does_not_establish: A currency fence on one key family. Collections move; the volume's 2010 printing is what the portion records, and the intake's own framing (museum-location resolution as printed) is the limit. Any product that needs current locations must source them elsewhere and say so; under this study the values function as corroborating keys (section 4.3) and coverage fill (section 4.4) only. They are a dated snapshot, used as join keys and field-fill, and are never stated as current locations.
falsifier: Any Spec 037 product stating a present-day location for an object on the portion's authority defeats this claim.
statement: Under Spec 037, museum/owner values from the portion stand as printed in 2010.

does_not_establish: The product-side coverage fence (C01 is the statement-side one). The portion is 31 pages of a volume whose published yield is 1,290 objects; its 2,101 distinct numbers exceed that figure because the portion also carries addenda and the HARP sequence - units that are not the volume's object count, as the intake recorded. H-1019's absence from the portion stands as found; the spine has no row for it and the gap is named, not papered over. The ranges are M-1660-M-2134 and H-1020-H-2590 plus addenda; no product of this study claims coverage of Vol. 3.1 as a whole or of any range outside the portion.
falsifier: Any product naming or describing the spine as covering the whole volume, or filling the H-1019 gap from another source, defeats this claim.
statement: The spine's coverage is the portion's ranges only.

does_not_establish: Scope claim for the whole spec. The registered prediction (docs/PREDICTION_REGISTER.md, PRED-2026-007) is the input, not a question; a verdict is a statement about the registered criterion over the population the registered definition covers. It does not govern the enumeration (C03-C04), the computation (C06-C07), or the register handling (C10). What ITM signs mean, and whether the Phase 5 clustering is the right carving of the script, are never judged under this spec (C12).
falsifier: Any Spec 038 outcome statement claiming more than the registered criterion's outcome over the enumerated population defeats this claim.
statement: A verdict under Spec 038 states only whether the registered criterion for PRED-2026-007 is met over the enumerated ITM population.

does_not_establish: The criterion claim (the register's, restated as the definition of the pass line). It does not govern how TERMINAL-cluster membership is determined (C06, DD-038-9), which signs are in the population (C03), or the coverage denominator (C07), each stated in its own claim. The verdict follows mechanically from the share against this bar (DD-038-1); no outcome is pre-written. The verdict mapping is part of the criterion as registered: CONFIRMED at 70% or above, NOT CONFIRMED below. The criterion, verbatim: at least 70% of ITM-coded signs are TERMINAL or cluster in TERMINAL clusters.
falsifier: Any Spec 038 product that applies any bar other than 70%, adds an inconclusive band, or carries the pre-execution 67% figure into a verdict defeats this claim.
statement: The success criterion is the registered one, carried verbatim.

does_not_establish: The population-frame claim (spec section 2 and section 3 check 0.1). The primary source is reports/indus_cgsa_cluster_analysis.json (data.a[].icit_function); the cross-check is data/crosswalks/canonical_sign_registry.csv (icit_function); the primary governs membership and cross-check disagreements are recorded, never silently applied. No sample, no frequency threshold, no attestation requirement. P098 (LOG) is excluded by this rule. The claim does not state the population's membership or size: those are execution-time facts (C13).
falsifier: Any Spec 038 product whose population includes a sign the primary source does not code exactly ITM, excludes one it does, or was drawn from a source other than the named primary under the stated conflict rule, defeats this claim.
statement: The population is every distinct sign whose function code in the primary source named at step 0 is exactly ITM.

does_not_establish: The step-0 order claim (spec section 3). No check is waived, sampled, or repaired by substitution, and no Phase 5 assignment is looked up before the enumeration is written and hashed. The census branch (C08) is not a step-0 failure and is governed by its own claim; the coverage rule (C07) governs scoring after step 0 passes. The order is: sources and provenance, enumeration with completeness checks, then Phase 5 output verification. A failed check closes the study as CANNOT BE RUN AS WRITTEN, unscored.
falsifier: Any Spec 038 execution that scores after a failed step-0 check, reorders the checks to reach a preferred result, or substitutes a source mid-run defeats this claim.
statement: Step 0 runs in the fixed order of spec section 3, fail-closed.

does_not_establish: The provenance claim (DD-038-2). The register's 'ICIT function codes (from mayig features)' line conflicts with the held files: the mayig feature files carry no function codes, and the programme's parser reads the codes from Wells-derived catalog lines. The reconciliation records what the primary source actually is and how the codes descend from that lineage. It changes no register text, no population membership (C03), and no criterion (C02). The register text itself is not edited under this spec.
falsifier: Any Spec 038 product that edits the registered section 3 text, or repeats the 'from mayig features' line as verified fact, defeats this claim.
statement: Under Spec 038, the provenance reconciliation is an appended dated note.

does_not_establish: The scoring-input claim (spec section 3 check 0.3, section 5; DD-038-9). Assignments come from outputs/analysis/sign_clusters.json; cluster classes from reports/cluster_characterization.md, the disclosed operationalisation for a quantity no recorded rule assigns. If the recorded output does not survive in sign-assignable form the study closes as CANNOT BE RUN AS WRITTEN. A fresh clustering under any settings is a new prediction's business. The claim does not assert the clustering is correct or stable (C11).
falsifier: Any Spec 038 execution that re-clusters, re-characterises, or derives a cluster class from rates computed at execution defeats this claim.
statement: Scoring reads the recorded CGSA Phase 5 output only, with a cluster's class taken from the recorded Phase 5 characterisation; no re-clustering is run.

does_not_establish: The coverage claim (spec section 6; DD-038-4). This rule is a design addition: the register specifies no denominator for unassigned signs, and the claim says so rather than attributing the rule to the register. Unassigned signs are never dropped from the frame (C03) and their existence is stated in the verdict's first sentence whenever the rule is engaged. The share is computed on the assigned population with coverage stated, unless the unassigned signs cannot change the outcome arithmetically; below 80% coverage without decisiveness, the test is recorded as run-at-partial-scope.
falsifier: Any Spec 038 verdict whose denominator differs from this rule, or that fails to state coverage in its first sentence when the rule is engaged, defeats this claim.
statement: The coverage rule is the design's, fixed in advance.

does_not_establish: The census-branch claim (spec section 6; DD-038-1). A completion, not a failure and not a step-0 closure (C14): the registered test has then been run at the only scope it ever had. No outcome for this branch is pre-written anywhere in this spec: the verdict is whatever the mechanical rule (C02, C07) yields over the enumerated population and the recorded assignments, and the register's recorded 67% - whose denominator mixed in a non-ITM sign - does not carry into it.
falsifier: Any Spec 038 product that states the census branch's outcome before the enumeration and the recorded assignments are read at execution, or that reports it as a failure or closure, defeats this claim.
statement: If the enumerated population is exactly the ITM signs already tested, the design closes with the census as its finding: a completion, scored at full scope by the mechanical verdict rule.

does_not_establish: The register-handling claim (spec section 7). Supersession is by append under section 6 of the register, in the same execution act as the provenance reconciliation append (C05), with the Phase D register-hash pin advanced by name for the authorised change. On a step-0 closure the section 3 Outcome stays PARTIALLY CONFIRMED as the pre-execution record (C14). No other prediction's state changes under this spec. The registered section 3 text is never edited and every other entry stays byte-identical.
falsifier: Any Spec 038 execution product that edits the registered section 3 text in place, or alters another prediction's entry, defeats this claim.
statement: The outcome is appended to the prediction register as a dated entry superseding the PARTIALLY CONFIRMED wording.

does_not_establish: The caveat claim (spec section 8). The programme's cross-compilation work shows sign treatment is contested, so cluster membership is weaker evidence than a bare percentage suggests. The design's answer is fidelity: the registered test named this clustering, so this clustering is scored (C06), and the caveat rides in the appended entry and every outcome statement. The claim does not itself assert the clustering is unstable to any stated degree. The named clustering is scored as recorded, and its contested stability is stated, not repaired.
falsifier: Any Spec 038 outcome statement that omits the stability caveat, or presents the verdict as settling the clustering's validity, defeats this claim.
statement: Every outcome statement under this spec carries the clustering-stability caveat.

does_not_establish: The non-establishment claim (spec section 9; D-31's own boundary). The study scores one registered prediction about one coding scheme inside one clustering. A CONFIRMED verdict would not validate the coding scheme's semantics or the clustering; a NOT CONFIRMED verdict would not refute either beyond the registered statement. Nor does any outcome under this spec establish that the Phase 5 clustering carves the script at its joints.
falsifier: Any Spec 038 outcome statement presenting the result as evidence about sign meanings or the clustering's correctness defeats this claim.
statement: No outcome under Spec 038 establishes that ITM signs mean anything terminal.

does_not_establish: The draft-stage claim. At drafting, the cited sources were verified by form and hash only: the primary source's icit_function values were not read across signs, no sign beyond the register's three named signs was looked up in the Phase 5 output, and no share was computed. Any number for the population size appearing in a draft-stage product would defeat this claim by construction. This draft enumerates nothing, scores nothing, and executes nothing. The population's size is likewise an execution-time fact.
falsifier: Any draft-stage Spec 038 product stating the ITM population's membership or size, or any share over it, defeats this claim.
statement: The population's membership is an execution-time fact that does not exist yet.

does_not_establish: The reporting claim (spec sections 6-7). A closure (CANNOT BE RUN AS WRITTEN) is not a refutation: PRED-2026-007 remains unscored by that execution and the register's section 4 gains no entry from it. The census completion (C08) is the opposite category: a scored completion at full scope. The two are never reported as each other. It is never reported as a verdict.
falsifier: Any Spec 038 product that reports a closure as a verdict or refutation, or the census completion as a failure, defeats this claim.
statement: A step-0 closure under Spec 038 is reported as a closure in its own reporting category.

does_not_establish: Scope claim for the whole spec. An assignment is a statement about the published record, made under the frozen mapping rule; it is not a dating of the site, not a stratigraphic finding, and not chronological evidence. It does not govern the evidence standard (C02-C04), the record's shape (C05-C12), or the verification step (C14), each stated in its own claim.
falsifier: Any Spec 039 product that presents an assigned label as a date, a dating, or chronological evidence for any site defeats this claim.
statement: An assignment under Spec 039 states only that a named publication assigns the site to the assigned period.

does_not_establish: The evidence-standard claim (the owner's Option 1, decided 2026-10-20). A determination is a publication's own period statement about the named site, cited with its locator. It does not govern what counts as published at the TwoRains edge (DD-039-3), the citation record's shape (C08), or the restricted-source posture (C08's boundary and spec section 3).
falsifier: Any assigned label whose recorded evidence contains no published period determination for that site defeats this claim.
statement: Every assigned period label rests on at least one published period determination for that site.

does_not_establish: The Option 2 exclusion, stated on its own because the spine is the tempting source: the program's extended spine (205 rows) holds dated contexts for many gazetteer sites, and a dates-to-period inference from it is exactly the program-derived assignment the owner declined. It does not govern the spine itself, which this act never modifies.
falsifier: Any assigned label whose recorded evidence cites a chronology-spine row, a calibrated range, or a date-derived rule defeats this claim.
statement: No period label is assigned from chronology-spine dates.

does_not_establish: The blank rule. The field stays null and the assignment report records the blank's reason code (NO_PUBLISHED_DETERMINATION, UNMAPPED_SCHEME_VALUE, or OUTSIDE_LABEL_SET). It does not govern contested sites, whose determinations exist and disagree (C09).
falsifier: Any site carrying an assignment while its recorded evidence set is empty defeats this claim.
statement: A site with no admissible published determination carries no assignment.

does_not_establish: The label-set claim, carrying DD-039-1's recommendation into the contract for the freeze decision. The vocabulary matches Spec 031's frozen period rule (F031-C10), which turns on Mature Harappan occupation and attempts no finer slicing. A published determination outside the Harappan sequence grounds no assignment under this set. The three labels are Early Harappan, Mature Harappan, and Late Harappan.
falsifier: Any assignment under this act carrying a label outside the three-label set defeats this claim.
statement: The label set is the DD-039-1 three-period set.

does_not_establish: The unit claim. The gazetteer holds 36 source-assertion rows over 30 program sites; the program's assignment is a statement about the site, written identically onto each of its rows, while every row keeps its own source's assertion untouched in all other fields (C11). It does not govern clustering, which this act never changes. The site-level assignment is carried onto every gazetteer row for that site.
falsifier: Any assigned gazetteer in which two rows sharing a program_site_id carry different assignment records defeats this claim.
statement: Assignments are made per program site.

does_not_establish: The section 6.2 field contract, carried verbatim in substance: program_period_assignment is nullable, and when present the mapping rule and the reviewer are recorded. The mapping rule named is an entry of the frozen scheme-aware mapping table (spec section 4). The pair consists of the mapping rule applied and the reviewer of record.
falsifier: Any assignment record lacking a mapping-rule identifier or a reviewer defeats this claim.
statement: Every assignment records its mapping-rule/reviewer pair.

does_not_establish: The traceability claim. Each evidence entry carries its source, citation, locator (page, table, or record), the period value as published, and its period scheme. For sources standing catalogue_only or open_access_read_only under Spec 027 section 5.1, the citation and the determination as published are recorded; the source's contents are not copied in bulk. The pair consists of the determination's citation and its locator.
falsifier: Any assignment whose evidence entries lack a citation or a locator for any determination it rests on defeats this claim.
statement: Every assignment records a citation/locator pair for each determination it rests on.

does_not_establish: The contested-flag claim. Both (or all) conflicting determinations stay on the record verbatim with their citations; the flag is part of the assignment record, and downstream consumers report both ways over contested assignments (spec section 5). It does not govern how a contest is resolved - under this act it is not resolved (C10).
falsifier: Any site whose recorded determinations map to more than one label while its assignment record carries no contested flag defeats this claim.
statement: A site whose admissible determinations map to more than one label is flagged contested.

does_not_establish: The section 6.3 rule, carried verbatim in substance: no majority vote silently resolves conflicting source rows. It also does not license resolution by source hierarchy: the hierarchy of DD-039-2 orders citation and presentation only. Spec 030 Ask 2 (whether a contested-excluded computation must bind a future Q6 freeze) is a different question, expressly reserved, and is neither decided nor used here.
falsifier: Any Spec 039 product in which a contested assignment is replaced by a single label on a count of sources defeats this claim.
statement: No contested assignment is resolved by majority vote.

does_not_establish: The append-only claim. Execution writes a new file (gazetteer_rows_assigned.jsonl) carrying all 36 rows; the pre-act file is not modified, its SHA-256 is pinned in the outcome record, and its original bytes - including every empty period field - remain in git history. A field-level diff of the two files outside program_period_assignment is empty.
falsifier: Any difference between the pre-act file and the assigned gazetteer in any field other than program_period_assignment defeats this claim.
statement: Every pre-act gazetteer field outside the assignment field is preserved unchanged in the assigned gazetteer.

does_not_establish: The publication claim. Record 23300361 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23300361) is a published deposit; execution deposits a new version carrying the assigned gazetteer for the releasable rows under v1's licence posture, and the existing version's files are never edited, replaced, or withdrawn by this act.
falsifier: Any modification of the existing deposit's files, metadata, or availability attributable to this act defeats this claim.
statement: The existing Stage 0 Zenodo deposit is superseded only by a new version of the same record.

does_not_establish: The no-verdict-change fence. Spec 031's closures (bead/craft NOT-YET-TESTABLE; ceramic NOT ESTIMABLE) and Spec 030's Q6 re-test results stand exactly as recorded; this act's assignments are inputs future studies may consume under their own freezes. It does not govern the verification re-computation, which issues no verdict (C14).
falsifier: Any record that amends, supersedes, or restates a Spec 030 or Spec 031 verdict on the basis of this act's assignments defeats this claim.
statement: No study verdict changes as a consequence of this act alone.

does_not_establish: The verification-scope claim (DD-039-5's recommendation, carried for the freeze decision). The step reads period eligibility under Spec 031's frozen rule (F031-C10) over the assigned gazetteer, reports eligible sites both ways over contested assignments, and then states the standing link-mass floor. No response is computed and no Spec 031 machinery beyond the margins first gate runs.
falsifier: Any execution under this act that computes a Q7 response, a similarity matrix, or a verdict defeats this claim.
statement: The margins verification step recomputes only the period-eligibility gate of the Phase-395 margins step.

does_not_establish: The unaffected-quantity claim, stated so no product of this act can imply the act moved it. The Phase-395 record fixes the quantities: link_eligible_sites_in_gazetteer = 2 (Harappa, Mohenjo-daro) and 1 linked pair in-universe, against frozen floors of 8 eligible sites and 10 linked pairs. Assignments change period labels only; links are provenance determinations, a different record entirely. It stands at 2 link-eligible sites and 1 linked pair both before and after the act.
falsifier: Any Spec 039 product reporting different in-universe link-mass figures as an effect of this act defeats this claim.
statement: In-universe link mass is unchanged by this act.

does_not_establish: Scope claim for the whole spec. The claim under test is STUDY-SPEC-025/G1 as recorded by Phase-140 and Phase-385. What any sign means, whether people moved, and every PRED-2026 question are outside this spec. It does not govern the dependency gate (C02), the assignment discipline (C04), or the computations (C05-C08), which are stated separately.
falsifier: Any Spec 040 outcome statement claiming more than the bounded G1 consequence on the ICIT-lineage layer defeats this claim.
statement: An outcome under Spec 040 states only whether the G1 site association survives coarse chronology control on the ICIT-lineage layer.

does_not_establish: The dependency claim (spec section 1). It requires Spec 039 executed, its freeze digest and outcome merged, and a hash-pinned machine-readable assignment artifact at site-period resolution with citations and contested flags. A site-level occupation label alone does not satisfy it. It does not govern how assignments are applied at execution (C04) or the execution-stage thinness gate (C12).
falsifier: A Spec 040 freeze record that names no merged Spec 039 execution, no assignment-artifact SHA-256, or only site-level labels defeats this claim and bars the freeze.
statement: Spec 040 cannot be frozen until Spec 039's executed period labels exist in the frozen site-period form this spec consumes.

does_not_establish: The population claim (spec section 6.1). Base population: 5,410 inscriptions at the 7 Phase-137 eligible sites from the pinned layer; sign columns fixed from that full population (count at least 10, rarer pooled to OTHER, placeholders 000/999 excluded). The analysis population is the assigned subset under C04; the column set is not re-derived on it. It does not govern period assignment (C04) or inference (C06-C07). Draft head carried verbatim: 'The primary test's base population and sign columns are the Phase-137 population and profile configuration reproduced exactly.' The sign-column clause of the draft head is governed with the population clause by this claim: the sign columns are the Phase-140 profile configuration, fixed from the full base population and never re-derived on the assigned subset (DD-040-4).
falsifier: Any Spec 040 product whose base population differs from 5,410 inscriptions at the 7 recorded sites, or whose sign columns are re-derived on the assigned subset, defeats this claim.
statement: The primary test's base population is the Phase-137 population reproduced exactly.

does_not_establish: The assignment claim (spec section 4). The mapping is keyed at site-period resolution over the inscription's recorded local chronological label; contested-only, ambiguous, missing, and transitional mappings leave the inscription UNASSIGNED in the primary. A site occupation label, a site radiocarbon date, the Phase-139 chron_band, and analyst judgement never place an inscription. It does not govern the contested sensitivity (C13), which uses the frozen sensitivity labels.
falsifier: Any Spec 040 primary stratum containing an inscription placed by site-label inheritance, by a spine date, by chron_band, or without a unique uncontested frozen mapping defeats this claim.
statement: An inscription enters a primary period stratum only through a unique uncontested published-determination mapping in the frozen Spec 039 artifact.

does_not_establish: The strata claim (spec sections 4 and 6.2). The stratum key is composition_stratum | preservation_class | period_stratum over the assigned population; site labels move only inside a stratum. Period enters by stratification, not as a regression covariate or matching score. It does not govern the statistic computed under the permutation (C06) or the interval estimator (C07). Draft head carried verbatim: 'The primary permutation respects composition, preservation, and period strata jointly.' The control strata named in the draft head are composition and preservation (the Phase-140 strata), with period added by this spec as the third stratum (DD-040-2).
falsifier: Any Spec 040 primary run that permutes a site label across a composition, preservation, or period boundary defeats this claim.
statement: The primary permutation holds period fixed jointly with the Spec 025 control strata.

does_not_establish: The inference claim (spec section 6.2). Pearson chi-square of the site x sign table as the divergence statistic; p = (1 + #{chi2_perm >= chi2_obs}) / (1 + B); Fisher-Yates via shuffle; no asymptotic p-value. The permutation p is reported with the outcome; under DD-040-1 it does not by itself mint the verdict, which C08-C11 assign from the interval. It does not govern the interval estimator (C07). Draft head carried verbatim: 'The primary statistic and permutation follow the Phase-140 configuration with 9,999 shuffles under seed 20261009.' The permutation clause of the draft head is governed with the statistic clause by this claim: the primary permutation runs 9,999 shuffles under seed 20261009 (spec section 6.2).
falsifier: Any Spec 040 primary product computed with a different statistic, shuffle count, seed, or p formula defeats this claim.
statement: The primary statistic follows the Phase-140 configuration.

does_not_establish: The interval claim (spec section 6.3). Inscriptions are resampled with replacement within the primary strata, stratum sizes preserved, B = 4,999, seed 20261012; both percentile and basic intervals are reported and the basic interval [2V - q97.5, 2V - q2.5] governs. It does not govern the margin the interval is judged against (C08).
falsifier: Any Spec 040 margin adjudication that uses the percentile interval, a different resampling unit, B, seed, or interval form defeats this claim.
statement: The governing effect interval is the Phase-385 v2 basic bootstrap interval for Cramer's V.

does_not_establish: The margin claim (spec section 6.4). The margin is the Spec 026 / Phase-385 declared practical floor for this result family, carried unchanged; it is a floor on the governing interval, not on the point estimate and not on the permutation p. It does not govern which outcome an interval position produces (C09-C11).
falsifier: Any Spec 040 adjudication against a margin other than V = 0.10, or against the point estimate instead of the governing interval, defeats this claim.
statement: The practical margin for the chronology-controlled effect is Cramer's V = 0.10.

does_not_establish: The supported consequence (spec section 6.4). It requires the basic interval's lower bound strictly above 0.10 after every gate has passed. The retirement is prospective and append-only: G1 reads SUPPORTED under control, chronology included, from that date; historical rider-carrying statements are not edited. It does not govern the straddle or below-margin consequences (C10-C11).
falsifier: Any Spec 040 record that retires the rider without a governing basic interval entirely above 0.10 defeats this claim.
statement: A governing interval lying entirely above 0.10 retires the chronology rider by appended record.

does_not_establish: The weakened consequence (spec section 6.4): lower bound at or below 0.10 and upper bound above 0.10. G1 is weakened, not contradicted: it remains supported under composition and preservation control and is not established under chronology control, with the drop from the Phase-385 interval reported. It does not govern the entirely-above or entirely-at-or-below positions (C09, C11).
falsifier: Any Spec 040 record that announces a straddling interval as SUPPORTED - CHRONOLOGY CONTROLLED, or as contradicted at the margin, defeats this claim.
statement: A governing interval straddling 0.10 restates G1 as a period-confounded association by appended record.

does_not_establish: The contradicted consequence (spec section 6.4): upper bound at or below 0.10 after every gate has passed. It defeats the claim that the site association survives holding time fixed, at the declared practical margin. It does not assert that no site association exists in any form, and it does not alter Phase-140's differently-controlled result. It does not govern the straddle position (C10). Draft head carried verbatim: 'A governing interval lying entirely at or below 0.10 contradicts the chronology-controlled form of G1 at the declared margin.' In the restated head, 'the margin' is the declared margin V = 0.10 (F040-C08) and the interval is the governing basic bootstrap interval (F040-C07). Second restatement at the same act: 'An interval entirely at or below the margin contradicts the chronology-controlled form of G1.' - the disjunctive form restated as the single upper-bound condition spec section 6.4 states.
falsifier: Any Spec 040 record that reports an entirely at-or-below-margin interval as supported or only weakened defeats this claim.
statement: An interval whose upper bound does not exceed the margin contradicts the chronology-controlled form of G1.

does_not_establish: The thinness claim (spec section 5). statement: A second program fits the redesigned shell without any change to shell text or structure, and creating a program requires only a name and a question (description optional).

falsifier: A render showing a log stream or history list with no window stated, or cumulative counts (e.g. lifetime error totals) presented as the service's current state.
statement: Every log or history surface in the redesign states its time window, and none presents cumulative history as current state.

falsifier: A digestion render whose rows lack the missing-act field, or any surface presenting a stage count/percentage as if it were understanding or settlement.
statement: Every row on the digestion board names the specific human act it is waiting for; no digestion surface shows a bare count or percentage as settlement.

falsifier: Any stage synonym in the renders (e.g. 'verified', 'approved', 'done') used as a stage name.
statement: Wherever digestion stages render, the five stage names appear verbatim: created, checked, explained, accepted, digested.

falsifier: Any protected route (route families enumerated from the built app: projects, spec-studies, studies, terminal, settings, shutdown, indus-evidence, jobs) answering anything other than 401 without a token or with a wrong token, or answering 401 to the install token.
statement: Every backend route outside the spec's open list (GET /api/v1/health, the built frontend bundle at /, /static/signs) rejects a missing or incorrect token with HTTP 401 for all methods and accepts the install token, with enforcement in middleware so any future route is protected by default.

falsifier: The token string found in any tracked file, any log line emitted during the test matrix, or any API response body; the token file existing with permissions broader than 0600 on POSIX; two generated tokens colliding or shorter than 43 characters.
statement: The install token is generated with a CSPRNG at no less than 256 bits, is stored only in the install data directory's api_token file (POSIX mode 0600) or in a process environment the operator set, and never appears in git, in any log, or in any API response.

falsifier: Any named consumer failing against an authed test instance: the tray's shutdown falling back to the kill path because of a 401, the healthcheck failing its identity check while the token file is present and resolvable, an MCP tool call rejected for a missing header the server should have sent.
statement: With the token in place, every named first-party consumer keeps working: the tray (health poll, shutdown, Open Glossa Lab handoff, Copy API Token), the supervision healthcheck's identity verification, the desktop verify path built on it, the in-repo MCP server, and the MCP skill client.

falsifier: The old token still accepted after rotation, the new token requiring a backend restart, rotation altering any file in the data directory other than api_token, or the rotate command's output containing the token value.
statement: Token rotation is atomic, takes effect without a backend restart or any data change, and immediately invalidates the old token: python -m glossa_lab.auth rotate replaces the file, the middleware's mtime-keyed re-read picks the new token up, and the command prints only the new fingerprint and the file path, never the value.

falsifier: The health payload containing any field beyond the identity set and the auth mode, the token or any credential material appearing in it, or /docs, /redoc, or /openapi.json answering 200 without the install token.
statement: GET /api/v1/health remains open and exposes only the served-identity fields (status, version, uptime_seconds, component, build) plus the auth mode word (auth: token or disabled) — no install data and no secret material — while /docs, /redoc, and /openapi.json require the token.

falsifier: Any other configuration — dev mode, a missing token file, a missing environment, an installed-mode variant — under which a protected route answers without the install token; or GLOSSA_API_AUTH=off taking effect without the startup warning and the health payload's auth: disabled report.
statement: There is no silent open state: the only configuration under which protected routes answer without the install token is GLOSSA_API_AUTH=off, which logs a startup warning naming the switch and is reported by the health payload as auth: disabled.

falsifier: Any account existing in the cloud identity store whose creation record is neither an invite redemption nor the first-run glassbreak setup; or a scripted registration attempt without a valid invite code that results in a created account or a usable session.
