statement: No account can be created in the cloud edition except by redeeming a valid invite code or through the one-time first-run setup that creates the glassbreak admin. There is no open registration path.

falsifier: Stopping and restarting the desktop backend mid-job, or a job going without heartbeat past the stall window, leaves the job in a non-terminal 'running' state past that window, or the job's record vanishes from the desktop dataset.
A job submitted through the hosted route being executed by Cloud Run Jobs or by any other separate cloud execution venue.
statement: A job started in the hosted edition reaches a terminal state — completed, or failed with the reason recorded — across ordinary desktop-backend restarts. Jobs execute in the resident engine of the Spec 080 production desktop install and their state lives in the desktop-resident dataset; they are never delegated to a separate cloud execution venue, never silently lost, and never hang in a false 'running' state past the application's stall window. (Revised by Amendment 5: Amendment 4's Cloud Run Jobs model is retired; the guarantee is restated for the resident desktop engine.)

falsifier: Any claim, digestion act, or study action performed by a signed-in test member whose stored record lacks that member's user id, or whose surface rendering omits the actor.
statement: Every act performed in the cloud edition — registering or explaining a claim, a digestion act, running a study or job, editing anchors or data — is recorded with the acting user's identity and displays that attribution on the relevant surfaces.

falsifier: Performing any listed action (login success or failure, invite create/redeem/revoke, role change, disable, removal, setup completion, hosted-route configuration change) and finding no corresponding audit entry with actor and timestamp.
An audit entry being modified or deleted through any application surface.
statement: Security-relevant events — logins (success and failure), invite creation/redemption/revocation, role changes, account disable/removal, the first-run setup, and hosted-route configuration changes — are written to an append-only audit log with actor and timestamp, readable in the admin dashboard and not editable through any application surface.

falsifier: A production bundle, manifest, bundle-store configuration, or hydration path for the hosted edition being created or used after Amendment 5.
The Status surface or the rollout record presenting a bundle id as the identity of the dataset being served, instead of the desktop install's revision/source commit and origin health.
statement: SUPERSEDED by Amendment 5 (2026-10-30): dataset versioning and atomic hydration are retired. No dataset bundle, manifest, bundle store, or hydration exists in the hosted edition, because project data is resident only on the Spec 080 production desktop install and is served in place through the edge/Tunnel route. The Status surface's bundle identity is replaced by the desktop install's revision/source commit and origin-health state (FR-013 as superseded; replacement tasks T057/T060). This claim is retained so the retirement is on the record, not silently dropped.

falsifier: A staging hostname resolving, or staging resources existing for this edition at any time — on Cloudflare (a staging Worker, D1 database, Tunnel, or VPC Service), on the desktop route, or in any Google Cloud Run service, job, or storage bucket created for this edition.
A glossa CNAME to a <UUID>.cfargotunnel.com target, a published Tunnel application for glossa.bitconcepts.tech, or any public route reaching the desktop backend except through the edge Worker.

The production route being opened for member use, or the glassbreak setup being completed, before the pre-launch proof record (claim-test results as amended, the C083-6 cloud-storage audit, the adversarial pass, the noindex checks, and the desktop-offline and bypass proofs) exists in the rollout record.
statement: Rollout is production-only (Amendment 2; decision D-7 cancelled): exactly one public hosted route exists, at glossa.bitconcepts.tech — a Worker Custom Domain whose edge reaches the desktop origin only through the named Tunnel's Workers VPC Service — and no staging hostname or staging resources are ever created. There is no published Tunnel application or cfargotunnel.com CNAME for the hostname, and no second public origin or bypass route to the desktop backend. The full flow is proven against a production-shaped local build and ephemeral preview deployments, and the route-specific proof battery (T059) passes on the assembled production route before it is opened for member use or the glassbreak setup prompt is issued; go-live follows the proofs directly and is recorded in the rollout record. (Revised by Amendment 5; Amendment 4's Google venue is retired and its go-live gate is dead.)

falsifier: Any resource in the desktop-resident dataset lacking a workspace assignment, or assigned in the initial scope reconciliation to any workspace other than the primary workspace.
The scope-reconciliation report's count for any resource class differing from the desktop dataset's count for that class.
Any unscoped project resource being served through the hosted route.
statement: Before the hosted route opens, a primary workspace named 'Indus Script' exists in the desktop-resident dataset and holds all existing project state: every project resource in the Spec 080 production desktop dataset is assigned to that workspace, the scope-reconciliation report's per-class counts match the desktop dataset's own counts exactly, and no resource is ever served unscoped through the hosted route. (Mechanism revised by Amendment 5: assignment is verified in the desktop dataset, replacing the first-publish mechanism.)

falsifier: A Member- or Guest-type account creating or archiving a workspace through any route or API.
Any surface of an archived workspace returning content to a non-admin user.
statement: Only global Admin and Owner accounts can create or archive workspaces. An archived workspace serves nothing: every one of its surfaces answers scoped 404 to non-admin users.

falsifier: A Viewer-role user mutating any content in that workspace, or a Member-role user changing workspace membership or settings, through any route.
A user exercising, in a second workspace, powers that derive only from a role they hold in a first workspace.
statement: A user's effective powers inside a workspace are exactly their per-workspace role, with global Admin/Owner holding implicit Workspace Admin: Viewers cannot mutate workspace content, Members cannot manage workspace membership or settings, and a role held in one workspace confers nothing in another.

falsifier: Any response to a user lacking a role in workspace W - including search results, list payloads, counts, and badges - containing any of W's resource identifiers, titles, or counts.
A direct request by such a user for any enumerated resource class of W returning anything other than a scoped 404 with no data.
statement: No cross-workspace leakage exists in any form: a user without a role in a workspace receives a scoped 404 for every resource class of that workspace (workspaces; claims and their records including digestion; evidence and sources; anchor sets and data surfaces; studies; experiments and analysis runs; jobs and results; discovery items; research-loop sessions; notebooks; reports; foundation status), and that workspace contributes nothing to their search results, lists, counts, or badges.

falsifier: The access view showing a workspace grant that does not exist in the identity store, or omitting one that does.
An access edit (grant, role change, or revocation) made in the dashboard not being reflected in the target user's enforcement on their next request.
statement: The admin dashboard's per-user workspace-access view is accurate and effective: it displays exactly the grants stored for that user (no phantom grants, none missing), and an edit made through it is the enforcement reality on the target user's next request.

falsifier: Redeeming the same code twice (two accounts or two sessions from one code), redeeming a code after its expiry, or redeeming a revoked code, in any case succeeds.
A plaintext invite code found in the identity database, in any log, or in any repository file.
statement: Invite codes are single-use, expiring (default 7 days from creation), and revocable by an admin at any time before redemption; codes are stored only as hashes, and a code that is used, expired, or revoked can never create an account.

falsifier: The setup route accepting a code, or serving its form, after the glassbreak admin exists; or a second admin being creatable through the setup path.

The glassbreak password, or any reversible form of it, found in chat records, repository files, deployment logs, or pipeline artifacts (the salted password hash in the identity database is the only permitted residue).
statement: The glassbreak admin is seeded exactly once, through a first-run setup gated by a single-use setup code that expires within 24 hours; the owner chooses the password himself on the setup screen, and no password or password-equivalent ever passes through chat, code, configuration, or logs. After setup completes, the setup path is permanently closed.

falsifier: Any data-bearing cloud route returning content to a request with no session, a forged session value, or an expired session.
A session belonging to a disabled or removed user continuing to authenticate after the disable/removal is recorded.
A session token readable from page JavaScript (cookie missing HttpOnly) or found unhashed in the identity database.

An anonymous request to any route outside the enumerated public surface (login, setup while open, invite acceptance, robots.txt, static shell assets) returning anything other than a redirect-to-login or a 401.

An anonymous fetch of the SPA shell or its assets whose payload contains project data - a dataset record, a workspace or program name drawn from the dataset, or a project count - as found by scanning anonymously fetched payloads against the desktop-resident dataset served through the hosted route.
statement: Every cloud-edition surface except login, invite redemption, the first-run setup (while open), robots.txt, and the static shell assets requires a valid user session; sessions are opaque, hashed at rest, cookie-carried with HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite, and are revoked immediately on logout, disable, or removal. The login wall is the deployment's protection (Amendment 2): for anonymous requests every other route returns a redirect-to-login or 401, and no project data - records, names, counts, or content-bearing payloads - is served anonymously in any form; the edge does not call the desktop origin for project data before authentication.

falsifier: A member session receiving anything other than 403 from any admin API, or anything other than a scoped 404 (with no workspace data) for a workspace the member holds no role in.
A member session successfully invoking the terminal, user management, invite management, workspace management, or any host-management action.
A Guest-type account holding, or being granted through any API, a per-workspace role above Viewer.
statement: Access is enforced on two axes on every request (Amendment 1): global user types (Owner - singular, the glassbreak account; Admin; Member; Guest, capped at Viewer) crossed with per-workspace roles (Owner/Admin/Member/Viewer/none), held independently per workspace. Admins manage users, invites, memberships, workspaces, and the terminal; members work only inside workspaces they hold a role in, see scoped 404s for workspaces they do not belong to, and cannot reach admin surfaces, other members' account data, or the terminal.

falsifier: Any project or research artifact, restricted marker, restricted-source filename, or scan/preview image found in D1, Worker storage, Cloudflare configuration, or any other cloud-side store created for the hosted edition.

Any anonymous, unauthenticated, or workspace-unauthorized request receiving restricted or project content through the hosted route, or an authenticated session receiving restricted content outside the desktop application's existing restrictions.
A production dataset bundle, bundle store, or hydration path being created or used for the hosted edition.
statement: No cloud dataset exists in the hosted edition. Project and research data are resident only on TRISTEN-DESKTOP, in the Spec 080 production install; the edge stores only accounts, invite and session records, workspace-access records, setup state, and audit data. Restricted material (the CISI class: scans and their derivatives) is never copied into D1, Worker storage, a bundle store, or any other cloud storage, and can be returned through the hosted route only inside an authenticated, workspace-authorized member session under the desktop application's existing restrictions. (Restated by Amendment 5: the publish pipeline and its bundle boundary are retired.)

falsifier: The standing header-check script finding any sampled response from either hostname (staging or production) — including an API error response and a static asset — without the X-Robots-Tag: noindex header, or a robots.txt that permits any path.
statement: Neither cloud hostname is indexable: every response carries X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow, robots.txt disallows everything, and all data surfaces sit behind the login wall. This holds until the owner lifts it by name.

falsifier: Presenting a desktop install token to the cloud edge (as cookie, Authorization header, or query value) yielding any authenticated access.
The edge-to-desktop-origin service credential appearing in any client-visible response, page source, log line, or repository file.

The desktop application treating a request as a cloud member on the strength of X-Glossa identity headers presented without the valid service credential (for example, a direct request to 127.0.0.1:8001 with forged identity headers).

The desktop backend being reachable through any public route that bypasses the edge — a published Tunnel application for the hostname, a glossa CNAME to a cfargotunnel.com target, or any other alternate origin path.
statement: User sessions are the only browser credential in the hosted edition. The Spec 082 per-install token is never accepted by the cloud edge, and identity reaches the desktop origin only through the edge: the edge terminates the session, strips client-supplied identity headers, and injects the authenticated identity plus a per-deployment service credential onto the Workers VPC Service binding request carried by the named Cloudflare Tunnel. The desktop application accepts that identity only when the service credential validates; the credential exists only in the Worker secret store and the desktop install's protected credential storage — never in a page, a response, or the repository. (Revised by Amendment 5: the hop is edge to desktop origin.)

falsifier: Any claim in the pinned regression set scoring differently through the hosted route than in local desktop use at the same AEE version, or the production desktop install resolving an AEE version outside the pinned >=1.5.0,<1.6 range.
statement: The cloud edition assesses claims with the same AEE library at the program's pinned version, through the same adapter code as the desktop app, so a claim's score means the same thing in both editions.

falsifier: The standing_position value in backend/glossa_lab/project_seeder.py differing from the fixture body in any character beyond trailing whitespace; or the fixture differing from the text the Spec 029 Phase E2 record carries.
statement: The program's standing position, as rendered on ProgramHome from the default project record, matches the approved fixture specs/084-policy-sync-conformance/fixtures/standing-position.txt exactly.

falsifier: ALREADY TRIGGERED as a finding: the live llms.txt (fetched 2026-10-31) names 'Zenodo v8 preprint (October 23, 2026), DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23604590' as the latest release. The claim stands HELD, not passed, until the corrected line is served.
statement: HELD — bitconcepts.tech/llms.txt names the current release: the v9 preprint and its version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23668053.

falsifier: DESIGNED, NOT EXECUTABLE: a fixture diff over those sources, once fixtures exist.
statement: HELD — The in-app Help text (HelpView) and the AI-settings data-flow copy (Settings panels) are owner-approved texts held as fixtures under this spec.

falsifier: ProgramHome.tsx no longer containing the fixture sentence (modulo whitespace), or containing a replacement framing that presents stage counts as progress toward decipherment.
statement: The stage-count framing sentence on ProgramHome matches the approved fixture fixtures/stage-count-framing.txt: the counts are an index into the anchor records, not a measure of decipherment.

falsifier: cloud/edge/src/worker.ts ROBOTS_TXT decoding to anything other than the fixture body, or cloud/edge/src/headers.ts NOINDEX_VALUE differing from the fixture; or either fixture edited without a recorded owner act lifting or amending the robots-away order.
statement: The cloud edge's robots.txt body and X-Robots-Tag value match the approved fixtures fixtures/edge-robots.txt and fixtures/edge-noindex.txt (disallow everything; 'noindex, nofollow'), per the owner's 2026-10-30 robots-away order and Spec 083 FR-007.

falsifier: Any fixture line absent from ApiToken.tsx (modulo whitespace); or UI copy appearing that contradicts the Spec 082 contract (e.g. offering to display or read the token).
statement: The API-token gate copy in ApiToken.tsx contains every approved string in fixtures/token-gate-copy.txt, so what the UI states about token handling (named 'API token needed' state, session-only storage, fingerprint-only display, the app cannot read the token file) stays the contract's text.

falsifier: Any fixture line absent from tray/glossa_tray/main.py (modulo whitespace); or tray copy appearing that misstates the supervision behaviour (e.g. promising a restart after a user stop).
statement: The tray's status and tooltip copy contains every approved string/template in fixtures/tray-status-copy.txt, so the tray's account of backend supervision (healthy line, stopped-by-you, auto-restart limit) stays in the wireframe-15 forms the owner ratified.

falsifier: The pattern 161 + (candidate|readings|anchors) found in any .ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx/.py source under frontend/src, cloud/edge/src, or backend/glossa_lab.
statement: No served surface in this repo carries the superseded '161' headline framing (161 candidate readings / 161 readings / 161 anchors, any case): the October 2026 audit superseded that headline set with the 94 strict core, and no app, edge, or backend-served text re-adopts it.

falsifier: A <RemovedName>.tsx/.ts file reappearing under frontend/src; an import of any removed component in frontend/src; or the string REAL_CATALOG_SUMMARY appearing in frontend/src.
statement: The Spec 081 D4-removed surfaces stay removed: no source file and no import for DeciphermentPanel, StudiesView, AG2Panel, AIChatView, CollaborationPanel, ExperimentRegistry, PhaseAdvancerPanel, SignDictionary, PresetsView, ExperimentsView, StudyBuilderView, or DashboardView exists in frontend/src, and the REAL_CATALOG_SUMMARY fallback-data symbol stays absent.

falsifier: DESIGNED, NOT YET EXECUTABLE: a fixture diff over frontend/src/cloud/pages.tsx finding any claims-bearing string differing from its fixture, once fixtures exist.
statement: HELD — The cloud anonymous-surface copy (login, glassbreak setup, invite acceptance) conforms to approved fixtures for its claims-bearing text (invitation-only statement, password-recovery posture, the setup audit-log statement, the invite issued-address binding).

falsifier: DESIGNED, NOT EXECUTABLE HERE: a served-page scan of the tracker finding standing text that contradicts the merged record (e.g. the pre-audit 'each supported by evidence independent' framing presented without its correction).
statement: HELD — The public research tracker's standing texts (bitconcepts.tech/research/ and /research/indus-script/: 'not deciphered' status, the corrected strict-core framing, the append-only corrections stance) conform to the program's approved record.

falsifier: a matrix cell or map element with no ledger id path, or whose content matches a non-ledger source (a sidecar file, a database row, a bundle) that no ledger entry mirrors.
statement: The ledger is the sole entry point downstream.** Every element of the generated matrix and the map traces to a ledger entry id, and no matrix cell or map element exists whose content came from anywhere else.

falsifier: a seeded divergence in any one class (a flipped ledger status not reflected in the matrix; a count mismatch; a hand-edited generated artifact) that merges with the job green.
statement: The verification gate guards the chain in CI.** A CI job beside C4 (`ledger-gate`) recomputes the matrix and the map from the ledger on every PR and push, running check classes V1–V9 (spec.md Point 4), and a divergence in any class fails the job.

falsifier: a negative-control run (seeded divergence) after which the published artifact differs by even one byte from its pre-run hash, or after which the build reports success.
statement: Publication is gated (adopted, Atlas note 2026-11-01).** Generated artifacts are published only through candidate → gate → replace: the builder writes a candidate, the gate runs against the candidate, and the published file is replaced only on ALL PASS; on a red gate the previously published artifact is byte-untouched and the build fails.

falsifier: a `--regen` run whose byte diff goes unreported, or a downstream defect closed by hand-editing a generated artifact anywhere in the repo's history after this spec lands.
statement: Lossless regeneration is a checked mode (adopted, Atlas note 2026-11-01).** The gate's `--regen` mode hashes the matrix and map artifacts, regenerates both from the ledger, and byte-compares; any diff is classified in the run record as exactly the intended change (named) or a downstream defect (fixed by regeneration, never by editing the artifact).

falsifier: commit order showing the engine predating the semantics/canonical registration; or a canonical scenario whose engine output differs from the registered expectation in any field, with the test green.
statement: Settling is derive-before-build (adopted, Atlas note 2026-11-01).** The settling semantics (`glossa-settle-1`) and the hand-derived canonical scenarios (with prose derivations) are registered in git **before** the settling engine module exists, and the engine's test requires exact reproduction of every canonical — counts, enumerations, and tallies equal.

falsifier: a reported settling number with no run record; an output surface missing the label; or a settling module importing a ledger write path, found by the V9 audit or by inspection.
statement: Settling is mechanical, labeled, and read-only against the ledger.** Every reported settling result comes from a stored run record (inputs incl. ledger build hash, rule version, per-rule outcomes, enumerations, coverage); every output surface carries the computation label (spec.md Point 3); and the settling package has no write path to the ledger (no intake/write module import — gate check V9).

falsifier: a comparison report whose two run records carry different input hashes; a comparison that narrates divergence without the per-claim list; or a touched claim with a pre-registered expectation the report neither names nor scores against.
statement: Interchangeability discipline for dual readings.** A dual-reading comparison records the same ledger build hash and the same corpus snapshot hash for both runs, and emits a per-claim divergence list (both bearing tallies shown per claim), naming any pre-registered expectation for a touched claim and reporting agreement or divergence against it.

falsifier: a store diff attributable to a settling run; or a displayed score differing from an independent ScoringEngine execution over the same relation set.
statement: Settling moves nothing.** A settling run creates only run records: no ledger entry, claim status, stage, score, anchor assignment, or store-of-record content changes as a result of a run; displayed scores are `aee/scoring.py` outputs over the ledger's relation set, never a parallel computation.

falsifier: a rendered count, element, or header value differing from the artifact/gate values for the same selection and build, found by Playwright + artifact comparison (Spec 081/083 verification precedent).
statement: The map renders the generated data exactly.** For any view and filter selection, the map's rendered counts and elements equal the gated map artifact's contents for the same selection, and its header state (claims by status, validated-anchor share, nearest dated items) equals the gate's recomputed values for the ledger build the artifact names.

falsifier: a generated artifact with no stamp, or a stale artifact displayed without its stale marking.
statement: Generated artifacts carry as-of stamps (D-D generalized).** Every generated artifact (matrix, map data, settling run records, any report citing claims) carries its generation time, the ledger content hash it was computed from, and the definition/rule versions in force; a surface showing an artifact whose stamp hash does not match the current ledger marks it stale.

falsifier: an out-of-scope record's element present in a scoped response, or a relation pointing at an element the response omits.
statement: The chain never widens visibility (Spec 083).** A workspace-scoped map response contains no element whose source record is out of scope for the requester, and no relation incident to an absent element. (Scope is whatever the source record's scoping is under Spec 083, as in C085-13.)

falsifier: a ledger line that fails schema validation while the validator passes it; or a seeded malformed entry the validator accepts in the Stage 1 teeth test.
statement: Intake is schema-pinned and validated.** Every line of `glossa-indus/ledger/claims.jsonl` validates against the pinned ledger schema (`ledger-schema v1`), and the Stage 1 validator, run in CI, rejects a malformed, extra-field, or missing-field entry.

falsifier: a claim whose status, stage, or verdict differs between its source of record before migration and its ledger mirror after, other than by a pre-existing adjudication act the reconciliation names.
statement: Scoping: this adoption changes no verdict.** This adoption changes no decipherment verdict, no claim's status or stage, no score, and the program's standing position; the migration reconciliation (per-population, before/after per claim id) is the evidence, and the Indus script remains not deciphered.

falsifier: a stage closeout recording a pattern improvement with no delivered note in the delivery record; or an incoming note (beginning with `PATTERN-NOTE-2026-11-01-gate-and-settle`, whose adoption README.md records) with no adoption record in this spec's repo record.
statement: Harmonization is exercised, not just cited.** Improvements found during this build (at minimum the two named in spec.md Point 7) are written as short pattern notes and delivered to the RCPH and Breaking-Point Atlas chats; incoming pattern notes are adopted with a recorded adoption act or surfaced to the owner as conflicts — never silently absorbed or silently dropped.

falsifier: two canonical entries with one fingerprint; an entry whose stored fingerprint differs from recomputation; or a seeded duplicate intake that is written.
statement: D-B dedupe is enforced at intake, not by memory.** Every canonical entry's `proposition_fingerprint` recomputes to its stored value under the frozen rules (`spec029-phase-i-v1`), no two canonical entries share a fingerprint, and an intake attempt whose fingerprint collides with an existing proposition is refused, naming both records, writing nothing.

falsifier: git history showing a modified (rather than appended) ledger line for an existing id, outside a D-E migration record that itself reconciles.
statement: Corrections are append-only reclassifications.** A superseded claim is marked by an appended reclassification entry with a `supersedes` pointer; no existing ledger line is ever edited in place.

falsifier: an entry whose falsifier or does-not-establish text appears in no source record and no human-authored record; or a gate run that omits the coverage count.
statement: No field is fabricated at migration or intake.** A migrated or intaken entry carries a `falsifier` or a `does_not_establish` line only where its source record carries one or a named human-authored record supplies one; where neither exists the field is null, and every gate run publishes the falsifier-coverage count of the ledger.

falsifier: an entry with explanation content whose named author has no adoption record, or whose author is not a named human; or a seeded authorless explanation the validator accepts.
statement: OD-2 authorship is preserved.** No ledger entry carries explanation content (`explanation_record`, or a `does_not_establish` line sourced from one) unless it names a human author whose adoption act exists in a durable record; the intake validator rejects explanation content without one.

falsifier: a regeneration diff over an unchanged ledger; or matrix content present that the generator, run on the same ledger, does not produce.
statement: The matrix is generated, never made.** `glossa-indus/matrix/matrix.json` and `matrix.md` are produced solely by the registered generator from the ledger; deleting them and regenerating from an unchanged ledger reproduces them byte-for-byte.

falsifier: a sampled non-empty cell with no rule id, or whose cited entries do not carry the stored relation its rule requires.
statement: Every matrix cell is traceable to its derivation.** Every non-empty cell names its relation, its citation ids, and the registered derivation rule (matrix-defs version) that produced it, and inspecting the cited ledger entries exhibits that rule's stored relation.

falsifier: a seeded Atlas-style miscarriage — a citation that exists and is relevant but satisfies no tie rule (e.g., citing Spec 054's UNEXECUTED closure as support for the Yadav claim) — that the gate passes; or any production cell/edge citation the gate's V4 check cannot tie.
statement: Citations carry their relations (adopted, Atlas note 2026-11-01).** For every citation on every non-empty matrix cell and every map edge, at least one registered tie mechanically holds (spec.md Point 4: T1 source membership, T2 dated test with matching outcome direction, T3 registered anchor, T4 registered instrument). Existence, shared documents, shared signs without a T3 anchor record, and topical relevance are not ties.

falsifier: a diff in glossa-indus/ledger/claims.jsonl or any freeze record attributable to a Spec 087 PR; or a claim status/stage in the app database changed by a stage's execution (S6 touches anchor sets only).
statement: This program changes no verdict, claim status, or ledger content.** No stage of Spec 087 alters an Indus claim's status, stage, or score, appends or edits a ledger entry, or modifies a frozen record; the claims ledger and the freeze records are byte-identical before and after the program. This does not establish: anything about the truth of any claim - the program is about the tool, not the decipherment.

falsifier: a seeded broken plugin module (import error in a fixture copy of the registry build) under which the suite still passes; or a registered count by category in the running system that differs from the pinned count while CI is green.
statement: Registry completeness is pinned, and a silent shrink fails CI.** A CI registry-completeness test pins the plugin module list (all 144 experiment_graph_*.py modules) and the registered node count by category; outside production leniency, a plugin module that fails to import fails the test loudly instead of shrinking the registry behind a log warning. This does not establish: that the pinned counts are the right counts - only that any change to them is a visible, recorded act rather than an accident.

falsifier: a live graph with a dangling atomicId after any stage; or a comparison run whose output bytes differ from its pinned pre-stage record in any field.
statement: Every live graph still resolves and runs with byte-identical results.** After each of S2 and S3, all 27 live graphs resolve every atomicId they reference, and the pinned comparison runs produce results byte-identical to their pre-stage records. This does not establish: that the graphs' results are correct - only that this program did not change them, which is the non-goal the owner set.

falsifier: a node in the manual reference that is not in the palette set; a palette node missing from it; a port or param in the manual that differs from the registry's; or a hand edit inside a generated block that CI accepts.
statement: The manual's node reference is the palette set, mechanically.** The generated node reference (user-manual block and the HelpView data module) lists exactly the palette set of claim C087-4, with each node's category, ports, and params as the registry states them; the CI conformance test of Stage S4 regenerates and diffs, failing on drift in either direction. This does not establish: that the surrounding prose is clear or complete - the claim covers the enumerable reference, the part that was mechanically false.

falsifier: a node in the default catalog response that is flagged legacy; a non-legacy registered node missing from it; or a palette-only id that exists in no registry.
statement: The palette is the registry minus legacy, mechanically.** The catalog endpoint's default response contains exactly the registered nodes not flagged legacy: GENERIC nodes, parameterized PARTIAL nodes, and the live working set. The palette set is computed from the registry and the flag, never maintained as a separate list. This does not establish: that the legacy classification of any individual node is correct - the classification of record is the census's, and reclassifying a node is a recorded stage act, not a consequence of this claim.

falsifier: a component test (or manual run) with the catalog endpoint failing in which the builder shows an empty palette with no error surface.
statement: A failed palette load is visible, never a silent empty.** When the Experiment Builder's catalog fetch fails, the builder renders an error state that names the failure; it never renders an empty palette indistinguishable from 'no nodes exist'. This does not establish: that the catalog endpoint is reliable - only that its failure can no longer masquerade as an empty registry.

falsifier: a merged PR that alters the pinned counts without a stage record naming the alteration; or runtime counts differing from the pin while CI is green.
statement: The registry changes only by recorded acts.** After S2's re-pin, the registered count and the per-category census in the completeness test change only through a Spec 087 stage PR that names the change in its stage record; the count never moves as a side effect of an unrelated change. This does not establish: that the registry should never grow - new primitives are welcome; this claim makes their arrival an act, not an accident.

falsifier: two importable definitions of one id in the tree; a fixture registering an already-registered id that the suite accepts; or fixture outputs showing the deleted definition's behaviour where the kept definition's was recorded as correct.
statement: No node id has two live definitions.** Exactly one definition of each node id is reachable in the built registry; the three shadowed classes of census Table 4 (IndusPhase254SemanticConstraint, IndusPhase255CommodityPhonemes, IndusPhase256LEExtension) are resolved to the behaviour-verified definition, the dead definition is deleted, and a duplicate-id registration in a test fixture fails the suite. This does not establish: that the kept definition computes the right science - only that there is one of it, chosen by a recorded behaviour diff, where before there were two and the choice was an import order.

falsifier: any of the 10 phantom names appearing in a manual surface while CI is green; or a generated experiment list whose count differs from the graph files on disk.
statement: No manual names a node or experiment that does not exist.** No manual surface (user-manual, USER_GUIDE, HelpView) names any of the 10 phantom node names of census Table 3, enforced by absence checks in the same CI conformance test; and USER_GUIDE's active-experiments list is generated from the graph files on disk (27 today), neither more nor fewer. This does not establish: that the manuals are well written - only that their enumerable claims about what exists are true.

falsifier: a converted node whose source still branches on a domain identity; or two parameter settings of a converted node that cannot reproduce the behaviours of the domain variants it replaced, on their pinned fixtures.
statement: A converted node carries its domain content in parameters, not in code.** For every node converted under disposition (a), the domain specifics (corpus, language, code table, weights) arrive as parameter or port data; the node's code contains no branch on a domain identity (a named language, corpus, scholar map, or sign list). This does not establish: that the primitive is elegant or complete - only that the domain content moved from code to data, which is the coupling property the owner directed.

falsifier: a module named node_registry.py in the tree after S1 without the recorded owner ruling for option (b); a broken /node-registry/ endpoint; or a document that still points a reader at the old name for the experiment registry.
statement: The Study Builder's schema module no longer impersonates the node registry.** After Stage S1, the module formerly named node_registry.py is renamed (study_node_registry.py) or, if the owner rules otherwise, carries a header and a docs entry stating it is the Study Builder's param-schema module; its endpoint (GET /node-registry/{node_type}/{ref_id}) answers unchanged, and both registries import in one process without ambiguity. This does not establish: that the two node systems should be merged - only that they stop sharing a name.

falsifier: documentation surfaces disagreeing about the bus's semantics; behaviour contradicting the statement (for the documented-ephemeral ruling: any surface promising delivery or replay; for a persistence ruling: an event emitted with no subscriber that is not later retrievable); or the pinning test removed while the statement remains.
statement: The events bus's persistence semantics are stated once, and the code matches the statement.** Exactly one documented statement (module docstring, user manual, and HelpView, in agreement) declares whether events are persisted or ephemeral-by-design and what a subscriber can rely on; the emit path's behaviour matches the statement, and the statement's presence is pinned by a test. This does not establish: that the ruled disposition is the ideal one - only that it is a decision, stated where a reader looks, and true of the code.

falsifier: a stored graph, ledger metadata entry, or test fixture referencing a wrapper id that resolved before S2 and fails to resolve after it.
statement: Legacy nodes stay resolvable; nothing stored dangles.** Every node id resolvable before Stage S2 remains resolvable after it, through the same ATOMIC_NODES table; the full registry (including legacy) is what graph loading, the metadata merge, and resolution consult. This does not establish: that legacy nodes produce current or correct results - only that history stays loadable. The _archive/ graphs are outside this claim (spec non-goals).

falsifier: a PARTIAL node with no disposition, with two, or whose disposition record lacks the evidence its class requires (for (c), any of the bar's three legs).
statement: Every PARTIAL domain node is triaged exactly once, on evidence.** Each of the 68 PARTIAL domain nodes of the census carries exactly one Stage S3 disposition - (a) converted to a generic primitive, (b) re-expressed as a composition of primitives in its consuming experiments, or (c) retained under the D3 bar - recorded in the triage record with its evidence; the domain-flavoured ids in live use are triaged first. This does not establish: that the dispositions are the best possible - only that each one exists, is singular, and is backed by the evidence its class demands.

falsifier: a deleted set whose (name, language, pairs content) differs from its group's kept set in any element; a distinct content with no surviving copy; a deletion performed by direct database write; or a removed id absent from the stage record.
statement: Anchor-set dedupe removes exact duplicates only, through the API, on the record.** Stage S6 deletes an anchor set only when another set with identical (name, language, pairs content) is kept; the earliest canonical copy of each distinct content survives; every deletion goes through DELETE /anchor-sets/{id}; and every removed id, with its group's kept id, is recorded in the stage record. This does not establish: that the surviving sets are good data - placeholder content that is distinct survives this stage by design; judging it is a separate act.

falsifier: a merged stage PR whose behaviour change has no corresponding manual change in the same PR, where the stage record does not name why no manual surface is affected.
statement: Manual updates land with the behaviour.** Every stage PR that changes user-visible behaviour updates the affected manual surfaces (user-manual, USER_GUIDE, HelpView as applicable) in the same PR; no stage merges with its manual update deferred to a later PR. This does not establish: that the updates are well written - only that they are not late, which is the failure F7 documents at scale.

falsifier: a shipped Logs surface missing a tab, a control, or a field the approved wireframes carry; a records tab that can mutate a record; or a Playwright comparison against the approved screens that fails while the stage is reported done.
statement: The Logs view is restored, to the approved wireframes.** The app carries a Logs surface with the two tabs of the owner-approved S5 wireframes package: a live stream tab consuming GET /terminal/log and GET /terminal/log/stream, and a records tab reading the jobs/job_results, phase_actions, and notification_log tables, read-only, with per-record detail expansion. The build matches the approved wireframes screen by screen under Playwright verification. This does not establish: that the terminal endpoints scale or that the SSE tail survives the cloud edge - the claim covers the desktop surface the wireframes draw.

falsifier: a taxonomy entry carrying a standing or status-class field for a node; or a study node whose standing text quotes or paraphrases a prose source rather than its derivation inputs.
statement: Where a study's standing exists only in prose — a stage record, a report, a spec's narrative — the builder does not read it: the study classes by derivation (C088-4) or as unjudged (C088-5), and the shortfall is emitted as a stale-bookkeeping find for the register. There is no curated-standing mechanism in the taxonomy format and no code path that accepts one; RCPH's source-and-token curated standings are expressly not adopted. This does not establish: that prose standings are wrong — several are the program's real history; only that they enter the picture through the register, where a human can judge them, not through the builder.

falsifier: a build accepting an undeclared domain or subdomain; or an assignment change in git history with no version bump and no stage-record entry in the same motion.
statement: Claim and study assignments live in one curated file, versioned program-map-taxonomy v1. The builder fails on a node whose domain or subdomain is not in the taxonomy's declared lists, and any change to an assignment is a new taxonomy version recorded in the spec's stage record in the same motion — never an unrecorded edit. This does not establish: that v1's groupings are final — only that grouping changes are acts with versions, not edits.

falsifier: page behaviour — a filter result, a search hit, a displayed count — that cannot be reproduced from program-map.json's fields alone; or standings logic in the page's script beyond filtering and searching the generated fields.
statement: The page's class filters and text search operate exclusively on fields present in program-map.json (title, standing, class, citations, domain, subdomain). The page computes no standing, class, or count that is not in the generated data; the per-domain counts it displays are the generated coverage block's. This does not establish: that the page is usable or attractive — only that it is a view of the generated data and nothing else.

falsifier: a published program-map artifact that differs from the gate's recomputation while the gate reports ALL PASS; a definitions change made in the builder's copy only that the gate accepts; or map artifacts published under a red gate.
statement: The Spec 086 gate gains class V10 (program-map equivalence): it recomputes the program map from the ledger and taxonomy by an independent route under the gate's own registered copies of program-map-defs v1 — not imported from the builder — and fails unless the recomputation equals the published artifacts, coverage is exact, citations resolve, and the as-of stamp matches the current ledger. A red V10 blocks publication of the map artifacts exactly as a red class blocks the matrix today. This does not establish: that the builder is correct — the gate is a second route to the same derivation, and agreement is consistency, not truth.

falsifier: a ledger diff attributable to a Spec 088 PR beyond the adoption append's lines; or a pre-existing entry whose fields differ after any stage.
statement: Across the whole spec, the ledger's diff is exactly the append of this spec's own claim bundle through `tools/ledger/import_bundle.py` at adoption, plus the regeneration of the generated layers that append forces. No stage appends, edits, or reclassifies any other entry, and no claim's status, stage, or score moves as a consequence of any stage: the map derives standings and never writes them back. This does not establish: anything about the truth of the appended claims — only that the ledger's one-way flow (Spec 086) survives this spec intact.

falsifier: a register entry marking an outside-reproduction gap closed, or a map edge typed independent, whose cited evidence is this program's own re-derivation; or an in-house result rendered without its type.
statement: In the map and the register, a relation or candidate is typed as in-house re-derivation or independent confirmation. A study or candidate that only re-derives in-house is never recorded as closing an outside-reproduction gap; the standing instance is WP4, whose eligible independent Parpola comparisons number 0 of 184 because the comparisons are circular. This does not establish: that in-house re-derivation is worthless — it is most of what the program has; only that it is not the other thing.

falsifier: a build that succeeds with a claim id or spec directory missing, duplicated, or assigned to two nodes; or a taxonomy entry naming an id or directory that does not exist, accepted silently.
statement: Every ledger claim id (857 today) is assigned to exactly one claim node and every spec directory (88 today) to exactly one study node, under the taxonomy. Duplicates, omissions, unknown ids, and unassigned directories each fail the build, with nothing written. This does not establish: that the taxonomy's assignments are the right groupings — only that they are total, singular, and enforced.

falsifier: an item on a named source list with no register entry and no recorded disposition when register v1 is presented for ratification.
statement: Gap register v1 contains at least one entry, or a recorded not-a-gap disposition, for every item on the registered source lists: GAP-C07; the GAP-C12 remnant; GAP-C13 (consolidating the per-study finds of C088-5); the repair brief's WP2 (linguist certification), WP3 (recomputation blockers), and WP5 (anchor-support residuals: 37 requires-revalidation, 3 expert-pending, 2 insufficient) items; Spec 086's residuals (matrix edges for the live population; the two-graph-worlds join at population one); the T201 mahadevan:64 derivation divergence; the 9-null-falsifier disposition question; the tracker llms.txt staleness; the desktop-clone sync state; the data-lineage owner question; and the 44 pending anchor readings. The consolidation task runs a completeness check that enumerates the source lists and fails on an unmapped item. This does not establish: that the register is complete in nature — only that it is complete against the program's own already-named lists, which is checkable.

falsifier: a study node whose class contradicts the roll-up over its members; a mixed study absent from the build record's judgment-call list; or a study class traceable to an editor's choice rather than the precedence or the recorded default.
statement: A study node's class is computed from its member claims' classes under program-map-defs v1's roll-up precedence. A study whose members are mixed positive and negative is emitted in the build record's judgment-call list with its member counts and the registered default class it is displayed under; no study class is assigned by hand. This does not establish: that the roll-up captures a study's importance or quality — only that its shown class is the mechanical consequence of its claims' standings, with the hard cases listed.

falsifier: two builds over identical inputs differing in any byte; or a stamp field that varies with build time.
statement: Identical inputs (ledger bytes, taxonomy version, defs version, spec tree) produce byte-identical program-map.json and page. The stamp carries only input-derived values — the ledger canonical hash, the ledger line count, the ledger's own latest entry date, and the defs and taxonomy versions — and no wall-clock time, per the Spec 086 stamp discipline. This does not establish: that the inputs are current — only that the outputs are a pure function of them, so staleness is detectable by stamp comparison.

falsifier: any rendered standing, class, or summary text for a restricted study beyond its name, its flag, and the registered name-only form.
statement: A study under a standing owner restriction (in v1: Spec 072, whose public naming is "executed — held under the Roif gate") appears in the generated artifacts as a node carrying its directory name, the restricted flag, and that registered name-only form — no derived standing text and no class chip. The restriction list lives in the taxonomy; adding a study to it is an amendment act. This does not establish: anything about the restricted study — that is precisely its function.

falsifier: a v1 program-map node with class in_flight; or in-flight status inferred from prose dates or stage-record language.
statement: Program-map-defs v1 registers the in_flight class with no derivation rule, because no record of record in the repository carries study run-state — job state lives in the live backend, outside the builder's inputs. No node carries in_flight in v1, and a build emitting one fails; running work is visible through the scans and the register, not the map, until a registered run-state source exists. This does not establish: that nothing is running — work is; only that the map does not claim to know it from records it cannot read.

falsifier: a committed program-map output that `--check` accepts while differing from a fresh build over the same inputs; or a merged Spec 088 PR whose diff edits a generated output without the corresponding input change.
statement: The program map JSON, the find list, and the page are produced only by the builder from the ledger, the taxonomy, program-map-defs, and the spec tree. A committed output that differs from a fresh build over the same inputs is caught by the CLI's `--check` mode, which exits nonzero naming the drifted output and writes nothing; no stage edits a generated output by hand. This does not establish: that the map's content is right — only that it is derived, and that drift is a failure, not an edit.

falsifier: a published program-map artifact whose stage record lacks a passing V10 run over it, or that predates V10's landing in CI.
statement: No program-map page or JSON is published — committed as a live artifact or served — before the gate's V10 class is live in CI over those artifacts. The build order in plan.md (defs, builder, gate extension, page) is a dependency, not a preference, and the page stage's record cites the V10 gate output over the page's own artifacts. This does not establish: that the gate makes the page true — only that the wider population never travels around the verification the narrower one has.

falsifier: any Spec 088 surface showing one aggregate progress number spanning domains.
statement: The builder's summary output and the artifacts' coverage blocks report node counts per domain, and per class within a domain. No output of the builder, gate, page, or register computes or displays a single cross-domain aggregate progress figure — no program-wide percent-supported, no single progress number. This does not establish: that per-domain counts summarize a domain's health — they are counts of nodes by class, nothing more.

falsifier: a claim node whose class differs from the table's output for its governing entry; a standing computed from a prose source; or an unregistered status string classified by inference instead of failing the build.
statement: A claim node's status class and standing text are computed from its governing ledger entry's fields (status, stage, falsifier presence) under the derivation table registered in program-map-defs v1, with reclassification chains resolved in ledger order before deriving. The builder reads no prose — no spec text, stage record, or narrative — for any standing, and a status string outside the registered table fails the build. This does not establish: that the derivation table is the right semantics — only that it is registered, total over the observed vocabulary, and the only route to a class.

falsifier: a bundle-less study shown with a derived class or a prose standing; or a bundle-less study missing from the emitted find list.
statement: A spec directory with no bundle claims in the ledger (28 today: the 001–025 directories and `026-core-research-source`) receives a study node of class unjudged — no derivation exists — and the builder emits one machine-generated find per such study into the build's find list, which the register stage consumes. The node shows no standing beyond the fact. This does not establish: that bundle-less studies are unimportant — several are load-bearing history; only that the ledger carries no claims to derive a standing from, which is GAP-C13's shape stated per study.

falsifier: a node in program-map.json with no citation, or whose ledger id or spec directory does not exist in the inputs.
statement: Every claim node carries its ledger id and every study node its spec directory name. Citations resolve against the ledger and the spec tree at build time and at gate time; a node whose citation does not resolve fails both. This does not establish: that the cited record carries the standing's weight — only that every standing names the record it was derived from, so a reader can open it.

falsifier: a scan report with a find outside the four kinds, or a candidate with no falsifier, accepted into the register.
statement: Each scan's finds are classified as exactly one of missing node, missing edge, thin evidence, or stale bookkeeping. Every candidate study a scan proposes carries a one-line falsifier. A scan output containing a fifth kind, an unclassified find, or a falsifier-less candidate fails the register stage's completeness check. This does not establish: that the scans found everything — only that what they found is in the registered shapes, each with its test stated.

falsifier: a settling or materialize-sets execution after which an earlier run record's bytes differ, the store census fell, or assignment-sets.json changed with no run record naming the regeneration.
statement: Extending semantics §9: a settling run reads only its pinned inputs, writes only its own run record (under its execution-minted id) and its run-index entry, and cannot modify, replace, or delete any earlier record. The run store's census is monotonic under run operations: `materialize-sets` and any other regeneration that today rewrites a shared artifact in place (`assignment-sets.json`) becomes a run with a record, and the artifact it produces names the producing run. This does not establish: that the engine's semantics changed — glossa-settle-1 is untouched; this is store discipline around it.

falsifier: an evidence citation in a merged record that names no run id and no legacy label, or whose named run record does not contain the cited number.
statement: Any number cited as evidence in a record of record names the run that produced it (run id) and that run's comparability key, or carries the legacy label of C089-17 when the producing run predates the run record. A number whose citation terminates in a summary of another summary — a stage record citing a chat summary citing a run — does not satisfy this claim. This does not establish: that the cited run's number is right — only that it is traceable to exactly one execution's record.

falsifier: a run store whose census decreases outside a recorded amendment act; a run record whose bytes change after its first commit; or a superseded run reachable only through git history.
statement: A run record, once written, is never edited or deleted by a later run. The settling run store's content-addressed overwrite (settling.py's `run_record_filename`: a same-basis rerun replaces its own record) is retired: a rerun writes a new record under its own execution-minted id. Where a later run supersedes an earlier one (the adoption-refresh pattern of Specs 087 and 088, where the superseded T405 pair left the store), the relation is recorded as a labeled supersedes link in the run index (decision D-089-3), and the superseded record remains in the store, addressable under its own id, with its own results. This does not establish: that superseded results are usable — a superseded run's results carry their supersession wherever they are cited (C089-4).

falsifier: a junction report or a pooled figure over a pair whose keys differ on a constitutive component; or a comparability refusal that cites a name rather than a key component.
statement: The same scenario name, the same test file, the same job or graph name does not make two runs comparable, and different names do not make them incomparable. Where two runs' keys differ on a comparable-constitutive component, the pair is reported as different experiments (with the differing component named), never as a divergence and never pooled. This does not establish: that name-identical runs are usually comparable — usually they are; the claim is that the key, not the name, is what decides.

falsifier: a gate run that mutates any store; or a quarantine whose only lifting evidence is a gate report.
statement: V11 follows the gate's standing discipline: it imports no write entry point (V9 audits this), produces only its report, and its red state blocks publication. Lifting a quarantine, ruling a junction explained, or reclassifying a pair as not-comparable are acts recorded in the run index by their named actors; the gate verifies the acts exist and are well-formed, and never performs them. This does not establish: that blocked publication is costless — it is the intended cost; the alternative is verdicts on unexplained divergence.

falsifier: a result-bearing execution on a named surface whose results are stored or cited with no run id, an id assigned after the results existed, or an id derived from the results' content; or a no-result execution with no run record.
statement: An execution is result-bearing when its output is written to a store of record or cited in a record of record. Every result-bearing execution on the program's named surfaces (settling runs, backend experiment jobs, study re-executions, suite runs cited as evidence) carries a run id minted by the executing tool when the execution starts, before its results exist, in the format registered in run-defs v1 (decision D-089-1). The id names the execution, not its content: two executions with identical inputs and identical results carry different ids. An execution that produces no results (a crash, an empty run, a refusal) still receives an id and a run record stating the absence. This does not establish: that the run was honest or correct — only that its results have exactly one execution to belong to.

falsifier: a pre-spec verdict re-opened by appeal to this spec; a legacy run record whose bytes were rewritten to add a key; or a post-spec citation of legacy results without the legacy label.
statement: Standing verdicts stand on their records: this spec re-opens none of them. Pre-spec run records are covered by index-only reach-back (decision D-089-5): each receives a run-index entry under a legacy id derived from its store path, carrying its recoverable key components and the label legacy — key partial where components (execution time, code version) are unrecoverable. A legacy run's results may be cited only under that label, and a citation that presents legacy results as fully bound falsifies this claim. The spec's force is prospective: new runs, and new citations of old results. This does not establish: that legacy results are suspect — most are the program's history; only that their binding is partial and must be shown as such.

falsifier: a ledger diff attributable to a Spec 089 PR beyond the adoption append's lines; or a run, index, or junction record written into claims.jsonl.
statement: Across the whole spec, the claims ledger's diff is exactly the append of this spec's own claim bundle through `tools/ledger/import_bundle.py` at adoption, plus the regeneration of the generated layers that append forces (the C088-15 pattern). Run records, run indexes, and junction reports live in their own stores; no stage adds a run kind to the ledger, and no claim's status, stage, or score moves as a consequence of any stage. This does not establish: anything about the appended claims' truth — only that the ledger's one-way flow survives this spec intact.

falsifier: a verdict, gate decision, or published number resting on one of two comparable divergent runs with no junction report in the record at the time of use.
statement: When two comparable runs (C089-9) differ in any verdict-bearing result field, or one yields results and the other yields none (absent, empty, refused, or crashed), a junction report (C089-12) is produced before either run's results are used for a verdict, a merge gate, a published number, or a claim adjudication. Use first and analysis later is the defect this spec exists to remove; the standing tray-flake adjudications (CI attempt 1 vs attempt 2 over one head SHA, five instances in three days) are the pattern this claim mechanizes. This does not establish: that divergence implies a defect in either run — it implies a question, and the junction is where the question is answered or quarantined (C089-13).

falsifier: a merged record citing experiment results with no job id; or a citation whose named job's recorded inputs do not match the inputs the cited result depends on.
statement: A backend job already receives an execution-minted id (uuid-based, `create_job`). When a job's results are cited in a record of record, the citation names the job id and the inputs the job ran over (graph id and version, parameters, data pins where the graph reads data), recorded in a repo-side run record at citation time. A result drawn from the live database with no job id, or from a job whose inputs were not recorded, is unbound and cannot ground a verdict. This does not establish: that the backend must change — the identity exists at execution; this claim binds it at citation, which is where it is currently lost.

falsifier: a verdict resting on a run under an open unexplained quarantine; or a quarantine lifted with no adjudication act in the record.
statement: While a junction's disposition is unexplained, both runs' results are quarantined: they may be cited only as quarantined (naming the junction report), never as support for a verdict, a gate, or a published number. Quarantine is a relation recorded in the run index, not a flag edited into either run record (C089-2). It is lifted or confirmed only by a recorded adjudication act: a named human's ruling on the junction report, or a further run under a stated key whose junction against the quarantined pair resolves the question. This does not establish: that quarantined results are wrong — only that their divergence is unexplained, which is disqualifying for verdict use until it is not.

falsifier: a divergence on a deterministic surface dispositioned as benign variation without a named difference; or evidence cited from a surface with no registered determinism class.
statement: run-defs v1 registers each named surface's determinism class: deterministic (settling under fixed pins; the generated-layer builders under fixed inputs), where comparable runs must agree byte-for-byte in their result blocks and any difference is a junction by definition; or named-nondeterministic (the suite, with the tray-flake family registered as a known nondeterminism; LM-bearing experiment jobs), where divergence is expected to occur and the junction's job is to show the divergence is inside the registered nondeterminism's shape — a teardown-error-only difference, a sampling difference — or quarantine the pair. A surface with no registered determinism class cannot have its runs cited as evidence until the class is registered. This does not establish: that registered nondeterminism excuses any divergence — the junction must still show the divergence matches the registered shape; a new shape is unexplained.

falsifier: a stage record citing suite results where the run left the tree dirty with regenerated claim files and no run record names the rewrite and its disposition; or a mid-run-precondition failure reported as a pass.
statement: A suite run's in-tree rewrites (the `extracted_claims` and `claim_reports` regenerations) are part of that run's record: the run record for a cited suite run states the tree state before and after, names any regenerated paths, and states their disposition (restored byte-identical to the committed inputs, or retained with the reason recorded). A check whose pristine-tree precondition is destroyed mid-run is reported not-run with the cause named — as today's records already do by convention — never passed. Suite evidence is citable only from a run whose record satisfies this claim. This does not establish: that the suite is deterministic — the tray-flake family is a named nondeterminism (C089-19); this claim governs the tree, not the outcomes.

falsifier: a verdict grounded on a regenerated artifact that carries no producing binding and no unbound label; or an artifact whose stated binding names a run that did not produce it.
statement: An artifact that is read as current (a generated layer, an assignment set, a cached extraction) carries or is accompanied by the identity of the run or build that produced it, in the stamp discipline the generated layers already use (input-derived pins). An artifact with no producing-run/build binding is labeled unbound wherever it is cited, and an unbound artifact cannot ground a verdict. This does not establish: freshness — a bound artifact can still be stale; staleness is detectable because the binding names what produced it and over which inputs.

falsifier: a verdict-bearing figure in a record of record that aggregates multiple runs without naming them, or that names runs whose comparability keys do not support the pooling claimed.
statement: Every verdict, census, stage record, report, and published number that rests on run results rests on named runs. An aggregate over more than one run names every run it pools and the comparability basis under which pooling is claimed (C089-9); a figure that silently pools — a pass count merged from two suite runs, a tally averaged over two settling runs — is a defect on discovery and is withdrawn to its per-run figures. This does not establish: that pooling is never legitimate — only that it is always declared, so a reader can unpick it.

falsifier: a junction report opened over a delivery-versus-record disagreement; or a run record cited as proof that a delivery was faithful.
statement: That protocol (owner order, 2026-11-04) governs presented results: a background-delivery presentation is a claim, never a result, and gate-deciding reads run in the foreground. This spec governs recorded executions. A fabricated delivery is not a run, creates no run record, and enters no junction; a run record certifies what an execution recorded, never that a presentation of it was honest. Where a presented result and a run record disagree, the record governs (standing rule) and the disagreement is a presentation defect under that protocol, not a junction under this spec. This does not establish: that the two defenses overlap in coverage — they are complementary by construction, and the gap between them (an honest delivery of a contaminated run) is exactly what this spec exists to close.

falsifier: a comparable divergent pair in a run store with no junction report; or an unexplained junction with no red-team section and no recorded scheduling of one.
statement: The junction report is produced by tooling when divergence is detected — at run completion against the run index's comparable predecessors, and by store scan at gate time — not by an operator remembering to ask. This is the owner's "extra scrutiny, perhaps an automatic red team analysis of the junction," operationalized in two tiers: the automatic mechanical junction (C089-12), produced for every triggering pair; and, for any junction whose disposition is unexplained, an adversarial red-team section appended to the junction report (candidate causes attacked in turn: input drift, code drift, environment drift, nondeterminism, record corruption, presentation artifact), each marked sustained or not on evidence. A comparable divergent pair with no junction report falsifies this claim whether or not anyone noticed the divergence. This does not establish: that software red-teams itself — the mechanical tier is automatic; the red-team tier is a structured adversarial record produced under the doctrine's standing red-team practice, and its depth is a human judgment the disposition records.

falsifier: a comparability judgment in any record that rests on components outside the registered key, or a run record whose key omits a registered component its surface has.
statement: run-defs v1 registers the comparability key: surface; command/tool and its version; code version (the git SHA of the tree executed); input pins (the per-surface hash list — for settling, the record's existing pins block); seed, where the surface has one; environment class (host/venue and runtime class). Every run record carries its full key. Two runs are comparable (the owner's "similar") exactly when their keys agree on the components run-defs v1 marks comparable-constitutive (decision D-089-4): surface, command/tool, input pins, and seed. Code version and environment class are recorded and diffed, and do not by themselves break comparability. This does not establish: that comparable runs must agree — agreement is the expectation the junction rule polices (C089-11), not a property of the key.

falsifier: a published artifact or a gate ALL PASS coexisting with any of (a)–(d) in the guarded set; or a run-defs change made in the tooling's copy only that the gate accepts.
statement: After the run-record machinery (S1–S3), the Spec 086 gate gains class V11 with its own registered copies of run-defs v1's checkable rules (never imported from the run tooling): it fails when (a) a published artifact in its guarded set lacks a producing-run/build binding or names a run that does not exist; (b) any record in its guarded set cites a run under an open unexplained quarantine as verdict support; (c) a run store's census disagrees with its run index, or a supersession link in the index does not resolve; (d) two comparable runs in a guarded store diverge with no junction report, or a junction report's disposition is outside the registered vocabulary. No run-produced artifact publishes around V11 once V11 is live over it (the C1 pattern of Spec 088). This does not establish: that the gate adjudicates junctions — it detects missing bindings, missing reports, and forbidden citations; adjudication stays a recorded act (C089-16).

falsifier: a junction report missing a named section, or carrying a disposition outside the registered vocabulary, or an explained-by-named-difference disposition that names a difference without evidence connecting it to the divergence.
statement: A junction report names both runs by id; diffs their comparability keys component by component; diffs their environment stamps; localizes the first divergent output field (the `_first_divergences` discipline of `run_settling.py`, generalized from expectation-comparison to run-vs-run, including the one-side-empty case, where the first divergence is the first result the non-empty side produced); and ends in exactly one disposition: explained-by-named-difference (naming the differing component and the evidence it caused the divergence), not-comparable (a constitutive component differs; the pair is reclassified under C089-10), identical-after-all (the reported difference was in presentation, not in the records — the report names the presentation artifact), or unexplained. This does not establish: that the mechanical diff finds the cause — it bounds the search; the unexplained disposition exists precisely for when it does not.

falsifier: a derived condition with no stated refuter; or a stated refuter that is not a record the record system admits (a scholarly consensus, a statistical trend, a document the system cannot hold).
statement: The derivation record states the observation that would refute the derivation's application: a record, of a kind the G1 record system admits, that the framework — the stated projection plus the derived condition — declares impossible, whose observation would falsify the derivation. The refuter is concrete enough that its occurrence would be recognizable in the record system (a named record kind with named properties), not a gesture at future evidence. This does not establish: that the condition is true — only that it is exposed to the records in the way D4 requires, so its standing can change on evidence.

falsifier: an asserted indistinguishability that no cited record or count supports; or a pair of states the account calls indistinguishable that a cited record does distinguish; or a distinguishable-on-the-record case, of a kind the account claims to cover, that it omits.
statement: The G1 document states what the records cannot distinguish, and every indistinguishability it asserts is tied to a named record or count in the program's own record: the signary's frame-dependence (Spec 077's frozen 557-sign population against the 64 distinct signs attested in the M77 corpus file and the 713 distinct codes of the ICIT frame); corpus-attested signs and contexts carrying no anchor coverage; the anchors register's 44 `pending_non_sa_validation` readings, whose validation chain is incomplete on the register's own face; and completions of the script that differ only outside the surviving records. This does not establish: that the indistinguishable states are equally plausible — equivalence under pi is a fact about the records, not a probability over decipherments, and the account assigns none.

falsifier: an outcome or stage record crediting this study with machinery from Specs 086–089; or describing the gate as adjudicating claims, writing artifacts, or doing anything its own header and the stage records do not support.
statement: Where the study's records address D6/S5, they cite the standing machinery as it operates: the append-only ledger; the matrix and maps generated from it by script; the gate (classes V1–V10) recomputing by an independent route and never writing, with publication only on ALL PASS; settling under glossa-settle-1. The account claims the machinery's existence and operation only as the Specs 086–089 records establish them, and credits Spec 090 with no part of building, extending, or repairing any of it. This does not establish: that D6's presence advances the instantiation question by itself — the scoping note already grants the element and still finds G1/G2 open; the matrix is the study's substrate, not its result.

falsifier: a closed S2 with neither a completed derivation nor a named obstruction; or an obstruction stated so generally ("the domain is too hard") that no successor could act on it.
statement: If no candidate's chain completes at S2, the stage record states the G2 outcome as NOT YET and names the obstruction: which premise fails, which step does not follow, or what the stated projection cannot support — specifically enough that a successor study knows what would have to change. No weaker statement is substituted and called derived, and no candidate is carried as "essentially derived." This does not establish: that the obstruction is permanent — NOT YET names missing work, and the skeleton records it as a publishable outcome, not as a refutation of the domain or the skeleton.

falsifier: a "necessary condition" whose derivation establishes it only over the observed corpus (an empirical regularity with a class-level label); or a statement whose quantifiers range over records rather than over states in classes.
statement: The derived statement N is claimed for every state in every projection-equivalence class consistent with the records, as the G1 document's projection defines the classes — a statement about what must hold in every completion of the records, not a regularity observed in the records that happen to survive. This does not establish: that N is interesting — a true but trivial N (an artifact of the definitions with no bite over candidate decipherments) satisfies the letter of this claim; whether N bites is part of what the derivation record must show and the outcome record must say plainly.

falsifier: a ledger diff attributable to a Spec 090 PR beyond the adoption append's lines; or an Indus claim reclassified, annotated, or re-scored citing this study.
statement: Across the whole spec, the claims ledger's diff is exactly the append of this spec's own claim bundle through `tools/ledger/import_bundle.py` at adoption, plus the regeneration of the generated layers that append forces (the C088-15 / C089-18 pattern).
