No stage adjudicates, reclassifies, annotates, or scores any claim; no claim about the Indus script changes status, stage, or score as a consequence of any stage; and the program's standing position (the Indus script is not deciphered) is untouched. This does not establish: anything about the appended claims' truth — only that the ledger's one-way flow survives this study intact.

falsifier: a sentence in the G1 document asserting an outcome (that an S element is met, that a necessary condition holds, that the study succeeded or failed at anything); or G2 content appearing in the G1 document's frozen version.
statement: Per the judging protocol, the G1 document contains the record system's definition, the projection rule, the cannot-distinguish account, and the absolute disposition — and no conclusions: no claim that the domain instantiates or fails any skeleton element, no G2 material, no outcome language. The study's conclusions live in the derivation record and the outcome record, which are separate artifacts. This does not establish: that a definitions-only document is neutral in effect — definitions decide what can be derived; the claim is only that the protocol's separation is kept, so a reader judges the definitions without the team's conclusions in hand.

falsifier: any record of this study describing it as a convergence step, a Stage 1 entry, or a dashboard item; or a stack change made in this study's name.
statement: Nothing in this study enters the program into VEXA convergence Stage 1, alters the program's local stack, or contributes a convergence-dashboard item. The study runs beside the program's stack as a registered study about the skeleton; if convergence later adopts the skeleton as a maintained form, that is a separate program act under its own gates, not a consequence recorded here. This does not establish: that convergence will or will not happen — only that this study is not it, per the commission's own boundary.

falsifier: a candidate absolute in the program's practice that the audit never considers — in particular an audit that never raises the frame question; or a disposition asserted without the exhibited variation or derivation it claims.
statement: The G1 document enumerates the candidate absolutes in the program's real practice — at minimum: the corpus frame a record set is read under (which sign inventory a corpus file's codes answer to); the anchor readings' external identifications (readings imported from named scholarship rather than derived from the records); and the surviving corpus's extent (what counts as the complete record set) — and disposes of each on the record: record-relative (shown to vary with the records, with the variation exhibited), derived (from the named absolute or from the records), or the named primitive absolute itself. This does not establish: that the enumerated candidates are the only conceivable absolutes — only that the ones the practice demonstrably uses were each faced and disposed of, which is what an audit is.

falsifier: G2 work begun with no G1 document on record; or the G1 content scattered across stage prose such that no single document can be handed to a reader; or a G1 document whose bytes changed after its freeze with no amendment act recorded.
statement: One document, in the spec's records (decision D-090-1), states Glossa's record system (D1), projection rule (D2), and primitive-absolute disposition (D3) in the skeleton's terms. It is written and frozen before any G2 derivation is attempted, and any later change to it is a new version under a recorded amendment act, so the document the G2 stage and any independent reader cite is identifiable by hash. This does not establish: that the document's definitions are right — only that exactly one citable document carries them, stated before results, as G1 requires.

falsifier: a record class the program's verdicts rest on that the definition omits; a provenance rule the class's actual records violate with the violators unaccounted; or a population figure in the document that the records at the cited state do not reproduce.
statement: The G1 document defines the record system over the classes the program's verdicts actually rest on — corpus records (the inscription files and their loaders), anchor records (the anchors register), and ledger claim lines — naming for each class what a record is, what provenance it carries, and its population counted from the records at the state read. A record that breaks its class's stated provenance rule is accounted for by the definition (named as an exception class with its count — as the anchors register's 3 `no_validation_record` entries require), never silently absorbed. This does not establish: that the records are complete or correct — only that the system the study reasons about is the system the program actually has, provenance rules and exceptions stated.

falsifier: an outcome record claiming any of G3–G5 as attempted, partially met, or met by this study; or program-history instances presented without their own records as though produced under this spec.
statement: No separator is computed or validated for G3 credit; no gate refusal or kill is staged or claimed for G4 credit; no reproduction materials are assembled or claimed for G5. Where the study's records touch standing instances from the program's history (the gate's recorded refusals, the matrix's regeneration checks), they cite them as program history with their own records, never as this study's G3/G4/G5 evidence. This does not establish: that G3–G5 are unattemptable later — they are commissioned in principle by the same order and sequenced after this study; this claim binds only what this spec does.

falsifier: two quantities in the G1 document both taken as given in absolute terms, whether or not both are called absolutes; a none-needed claim coexisting with an input the document uses absolutely and never derives; or a demotion of a candidate absolute with no derivation or record-relative account behind it.
statement: The G1 document either (a) names exactly one primitive absolute in D3's sense — a quantity taken as given in absolute terms, not relative to the records — with the audit showing every other absolute-looking input to be record-relative or derived from the named one; or (b) proves none is needed, by exhibiting each candidate absolute as record-relative or derived. If the audit finds the domain requires two, the document says so, and the study records a skeleton mismatch (under D3 the domain then does not instantiate this skeleton); it does not force a fit by demoting one absolute without argument. This does not establish: which outcome obtains — the claim binds the discipline (at most one, audited), and binds it identically whether the answer is one, none, or a mismatch.

falsifier: a derivation step whose justification is a physics theorem or the physics instantiation's example; or a chain step that follows from nothing stated (a gap presented as a step).
statement: The G2 derivation record shows its chain step by step, and every step follows from the skeleton's definitions and the G1 document's stated projection rule, record-system definition, and absolute disposition. No step cites a physics result — no F0 theorem, no separator result, no identifiability result about causal sets or order-and-count observables — as a premise. A candidate whose chain needs such a premise is recorded as not derived, with the step named. This does not establish: that a physics-*suggested* candidate is barred — the analogy may occasion a candidate; the claim binds the derivation, which must stand with the physics premise removed.

falsifier: a stated "projection" that names no mapping from states to records (a narrative about interpretation, a metaphor of projection); or two states the document calls projection-equivalent that produce different records under its own rule; or an equivalence question the document's rule cannot decide either way.
statement: The G1 document defines the candidate system state for the decipherment domain and states a rule pi mapping a candidate state to the records it would produce, precisely enough that, given two named candidate states, whether pi distinguishes them is decidable from the stated rule alone — not from the drafters' intuition about the states. This does not establish: that the stated rule is the right projection for the domain — only that it is a rule in D2's sense, which is what makes equivalence classes, and therefore G2, possible at all.

falsifier: the study closing with no outcome record; an outcome stated in vocabulary the skeleton does not define (a "partial instantiation," a percentage) without mapping to its terms; or no report delivered to the VEXA chat after the outcome record lands.
statement: The study closes with an outcome record stating the per-stage outcomes (G1: STATED or NOT YET with the missing element named; G2: DERIVED or NOT YET with the obstruction named) and the study-level outcome as spec.md defines it (INSTANTIATES-path, ANALOGY with the metaphorical element named, or NOT YET with the missing work stated), each with evidence pointers to the stage records. The outcome — or, if a stage cannot run, the blocker — is reported to the VEXA chat for the improvement registry, as the commission requires. The formal verdict over the full G1–G5 bar belongs to the independent reader under the judging protocol; this study does not issue it. This does not establish: that the reported outcome is the final verdict on the domain — the reader's verdict under the protocol, and the G3–G5 follow-on, both stand after it.

falsifier: PRIVACY_STATEMENT in backend/glossa_lab/privacy_statement.py differing from the fixture body in any character beyond trailing whitespace; or GET /api/v1/privacy not being registered in backend/glossa_lab/main.py.

Any file under frontend/src, cloud/edge/src or backend/glossa_lab containing the superseded draft placeholder '[UNVERIFIED', or frontend/src carrying a baked copy of the statement (its distinctive sentences) instead of rendering the served text.
statement: The app's privacy / data-handling statement, served by GET /api/v1/privacy from backend/glossa_lab/privacy_statement.py and rendered in the SPA's Privacy view, matches the approved fixture specs/084-policy-sync-conformance/fixtures/privacy-data-handling.txt exactly (owner approval 2026-11-05), and no served source carries the superseded draft placeholder text.

falsifier: an accepted statement of this form whose population, controls, or premise citation is absent; or one that survives in the records after C093-1's standing for its field has fallen, unstated at the fallen strength.
statement: A statement this spec accepts about how inscription behavior conditions on a culture-side field (for example: sequence length or sign-choice distributions differing by site or by material class beyond the registered controls) is stated as a fact about the joint distribution of the two projections over the named population, and carries C093-1's recorded standing as a premise on its face. This does not establish: anything about why the regularity holds — no reading, function, or historical cause is asserted by a distributional statement, and none may be read into one.

falsifier: a comparison result in any stage record whose register entry is absent, postdates the computation, or lacks any of (i)–(iv).
statement: A cross-cultural comparison is computed under this spec only if a comparanda-register entry naming (i) the comparanda set, (ii) the transmission mechanism — documented trade, contact, or continuity, stated as a checkable historical claim with its source, (iii) a fixed time window, and (iv) the practice compared, was committed before the computation's first run. Wide windows (centuries to millennia) are admissible only where the entry's mechanism is a continuity claim stated at that span; a window's width is never a substitute for its mechanism. This does not establish: that a registered comparison is a good comparison — only that it was fixed before it met the data, which is what makes its outcome a test rather than a fit.

falsifier: an existing claim's status, stage, or score changed with this spec cited as the act; or a stage record stating a reading, a sign value, or a language identification as supported by this spec's work.
statement: No act under this spec adjudicates, reclassifies, annotates, or scores any claim already in the ledger; no Indus claim changes status, stage, or score citing this spec; the program's standing position (the Indus script is not deciphered) is untouched, and nothing in this spec is a decipherment claim, evidence for a reading, or a step that presupposes one. This does not establish: anything about the existing claims — only that this spec's front is additive and its boundary is where it says it is.

falsifier: a GR-093 entry missing any of the four elements, exhibited by entry id; or a completeness check that passes over such an entry.
statement: Each entry in this spec's gap register (Stage 6, extending the Spec 088 register's discipline to the culture-side unknowns: GR-093 series) states, on its face: what is not known; a falsifier — the observation that would close or break the entry's present statement; an acceptance test — the administration whose outcome would discharge the entry; and an honesty-rule type in the register's existing vocabulary. An entry lacking any of the four is not an entry, and the register's completeness check counts it as a failure. This does not establish: that the register enumerates all culture-side unknowns there are — only that every entry it carries is stated in the shape that lets it be closed honestly.

falsifier: a matrix cell, map node, or derived statement in the material-context layer carrying no ledger id, or citing an id the ledger does not contain; a hand-edit to a generated file attributable to this spec; a ledger diff attributable to this spec beyond ratified intakes.
statement: Culture-side claims enter the system only as claims in the append-only ledger (the family this spec adds at adoption, C093-1 onward), entered through the sanctioned intake. The matrix rows and the program-map layer for the material-context domain are generated from the ledger by the registered generators; no culture-side statement appears in the matrix, on the map, or in any derived surface that is not a ledger claim cited by its id; no generated file is hand-edited. This spec's ledger diff across its whole life is its adoption intake plus the claim appends its later stages ratify one by one. This does not establish: that the ledger's claims are true — only that the one-way flow (ledger → matrix → map) this program's publication discipline rests on survives the new domain intact.

falsifier: a CISI scan or other restricted source material present in the repository or in any stage output; a redistribution of restricted content rather than statistics or metadata; or a contact record to the barred person attributable to this spec.
statement: CISI enters this spec only as statistics and data-list metadata lawfully held and publishable under the standing restriction (scans never redistributed, never in the repository); the Laursen author copy never enters the repository (the rebuilt Table 1 is the artifact); no stage act contacts Andreas Fuls, and no stage act creates an account or channel in any person's name. This does not establish: anything about the restrictions themselves — only that this spec's design never needs to touch them.

falsifier: a stage outcome recorded as accepted over a fired floor; or a floor, threshold, or population in a stage record differing from its freeze without a superseding freeze that voids the earlier runs.
statement: Where a stage's frozen floors fire — a joint population below its floor, a held-out arm the counts cannot carry (the inventory names the standing case: four of six named sites in the sequence-bearing subset carry 7 or fewer records), a join that fails its audit — the stage records NOT YET (the administration ran and did not meet its bar, obstruction named) or CANNOT BE ADMINISTERED (the frozen administration cannot be run, forcing counts shown) and stops. No threshold, floor, population, or case is adjusted under this spec to convert a stop into a pass. This does not establish: that a stopped stage was badly designed — the floors are the price of the acceptance machinery meaning anything, and a stop is a finding about the record system's present contents. ## The join, the restrictions, and the one truth store

falsifier: a consumed join pair the frozen procedure does not produce; or a pass whose join audit record is absent, or whose stated precision is below the frozen floor, with the pass nevertheless run.
statement: Any identification of a snapshot museum record with a text-bearing record (by accession number, holding, catalogue identity, or published concordance) that a Stage 4 pass consumes was produced by a join procedure frozen at Stage 1 and audited on a hand-checked sample whose size and measured precision the audit record states. A pass resting on an unaudited join, or on a join whose measured precision falls below its freeze's floor, does not run; the stage records the stop under C093-8. This does not establish: that an audited join is correct pair by pair — precision on a sample is the claim, and the audit's sample and errors are part of the record a reader judges.

falsifier: one snapshot record, exhibited by `glossa_id`, carrying a non-empty `canonical_grapheme_ids` list and a non-empty `material`; or a Stage 4 pass whose population includes a record pair no audited join produced.
statement: Within the corpus snapshot as pinned, the records carrying both a recorded sequence and a non-empty material number **0**, and the records carrying both a recorded sequence and a non-empty site_name number **966**, all in the indusscript-m77 subset. No Stage 4 pass may consume a joint population the snapshot does not contain: a material-side pass over sequences runs only on a Stage 1 join that has passed its audit (C093-9), and a site-side pass runs only on the populations the freeze enumerates. This does not establish: that the underlying objects lack materials or sites in the world — only that this record system does not carry the joint fact, which is the constraint the design answers to. ## Comparanda and acceptance discipline

falsifier: a culture-side field, in the census's sense, present in a named source and absent from the census — exhibited by file, key, and one record carrying it.
statement: The grounding record's field census covers every culture-side field present in its named sources (the corpus snapshot, the M77 and ICIT flat files, the CISI coded subset's loader, the three contact-zone rebuild files, and the corpus-catalogue seeder): each field a named source carries that names site, material, artifact type or typology, holding or provenance, find context, period, or execution medium appears in the census with its presence count, or the census names the field and states why it is not culture-side. This does not establish: that the census's sources are all the culture-side data the program holds anywhere — the claim is bounded to the named sources, and a source outside the list is Stage 1's to add by amendment, with the census re-run.

falsifier: the spec closing with no outcome record; an outcome stated in vocabulary §5 does not define without mapping to its terms; or no report delivered after the outcome record lands.
statement: The spec closes with an outcome record stating, per stage and in the vocabulary of spec.md §5, what was administered, what was accepted, what stopped and at what counts; and the outcome is reported to the VEXA chat for the improvement registry as a closeout deliverable, in the outcome record's own words. This does not establish: that the reported outcome settles the channel question — later stages, later joins, and the reader stand after it.

falsifier: a cited result computed under an entry whose terms differ from the terms frozen when it ran; or an amended entry whose predecessor's results survive anywhere in the spec's records as live.
statement: A comparanda entry's window, set, mechanism, or compared practice, once any computation under it has run, may be changed only by a new entry that supersedes it; every result computed under the superseded entry is voided in the same act and may not be cited, including in the superseding entry's rationale. This does not establish: that the original windows were well chosen — only that the register's history is append-only, so a reader can see every window that was ever tried.

falsifier: a statable rule or fitted predictor, frozen before its administration, that recovers a registered culture-side field from sequence-table-plus-bookkeeping features at or above the freeze's stated bar on held-out objects — the channel, for that field, is the same information re-expressed, and C093-1 falls for that field (the outcome record names the field).
statement: A candidate state in G1 §2.1's sense determines, for each inscribed object, both its text (the sequence the record system's coded corpora carry) and its material-context tuple as this spec defines it at Stage 2: the per-object recorded values of site, material class, artifact type, holding/provenance, and find context, under the vocabularies the Stage 1 normalization registers. The channel claim is that this tuple is not a function of the object's sequence table together with the record system's bookkeeping (source system, frame, derivation): there is no rule, statable in advance of Stage 2's freeze, that computes the tuple from the table and the bookkeeping alone. Stage 2 administers exactly this: a pre-registered prediction test in which the frozen culture-side fields are predicted from table-plus-bookkeeping features under permutation controls, and the channel stands as independent only at the strength the audited outcome records (spec.md §5's vocabulary). This does not establish: that the channel, where independent, carries information about any reading, sign value, or language identification — independence is a claim about projections of the state, not about what either projection says. Condition 1 (Spec 090, DERIVED) is untouched: this claim asserts a second projection exists to be tested; it does not assert the second projection separates any pair of states.

falsifier: an accepted pass in any stage record lacking its registered controls' run records, or resting on a bar absent from its freeze.
statement: A Stage 4 pass is accepted only if its frozen design's negative controls (permutation or shuffle of the culture-side labels within the strata the design names) and its replication arm (held-out sites where the design names them, and the inventory's counts allow them) were run under Spec 089 run discipline and the audited comparison of pass against controls meets the freeze's bar. A pass whose controls were not run, or whose bar was set after its first run, is recorded as NOT YET with the obstruction named, whatever its uncontrolled numbers look like. This does not establish: that a pass meeting its bar is true in the world — only that it survived the controls this program requires before a number may be cited.

falsifier: a register entry marked closed whose workstream's closure condition is unmet on the records; or a workstream at its end with its register entry unamended.
statement: At each workstream's end, its register entry (GR-088-01, GR-088-02, GR-088-03) is amended, append-only per the register's own discipline, to its measured end state: closed (its candidate executed and its closure condition met on the records), re-registered structural (its falsifier's structural outcome produced), or still open with the blocking fact named. This spec's completion alone closes no entry.

falsifier: a coded reading whose coder is a member of the derivation lineage; coding filed after recorded exposure to the project readings or classifications; or an eligibility recomputation resting on coding with no blinding protocol on record.
statement: The readings used by the eligibility recomputation are coded from the primary sources named by the locator record by a coder who did not derive the project readings, under the blinding protocol filed before coding starts (decision D-091-2: the coder sees the primary sources and the sign list, never the project readings or the WP4 classifications, until the coding is filed). The protocol, the coder's identity and lineage exclusion, and any deviation are on record; a deviation voids the coding it touches.

falsifier: an entry in the locator record with neither an entry-level locator nor a documented not-found search; or a pass census below 184.
statement: Every entry of the Mahadevan-Parpola crosswalk (v2.1, 184 entries) carries, in the locator record this spec produces, an entry-level primary-source locator for its reading fields (phonetic and semantic), or a recorded locator-not-found outcome backed by a documented search (sources consulted, in order, with dates). File-level citations do not satisfy this claim. No entry is left unexamined: the pass's census is 184 examined of 184.

falsifier: a stage artifact of this spec that alters a proposed reading or a ledger claim verdict, or prose in a record of record presenting a support-class or eligibility change as a reading confirmation.
statement: No stage of this spec changes any anchor's proposed reading, any claim's verdict in the ledger, or the program's standing position that the Indus script is not deciphered. The only quantities that move are support classes, eligibility classes, and validation statuses.

falsifier: a published artifact, after the recomputation lands, citing crosswalk agreement as independent support for an entry classified project-derived, used-in-construction, unverified, or ineligible; or a citation of crosswalk agreement carrying no class.
statement: After W1's recomputation lands, no published layer of the program (matrix, map, tracker, preprint prose) cites a 'Parpola agrees' relation as independent validation for an entry outside the eligible set; every citation of crosswalk agreement carries the entry's eligibility class. Before W1 lands, the standing class of every entry is its WP4 class, under which no entry is eligible, and citations are bound by that.

falsifier: a published artifact, after adoption, citing any of the 46 as confirmed or independently supported, or stating the core's independently supported mass as 94 (or as any number other than the measured count of record).
statement: From this spec's adoption onward, every published layer that cites any of the 46 internal-only anchors cites it as internal-only, and every statement of the strict core's independently supported mass states the measured number, not 94. This obligation binds from adoption, not from W2's completion.

falsifier: an eligibility count that differs from the mechanical recomputation over the locator and coding records; or a structural re-registration filed while at least one entry carries an independently sourced reading under the recomputation.
statement: Eligibility is recomputed mechanically from the locator record and the independent coding under WP4's classification rules (extended only by new versioned artifacts, never by editing the frozen provenance file). The resulting count is reported as produced, including zero: if the locator pass finds every entry's reading traceable to the project's own derivation, the eligible count stays 0 and the gap re-registers as structural (no independent Parpola comparison exists to be had from this crosswalk), not as an unfinished task (register falsifier of GR-088-01).

falsifier: an anchor counted independently supported whose support lines on record are all same-lineage; or a supported count that differs from 6 + (anchors with filed external lines).
statement: A per-anchor disposition changes from internal-only to independently supported solely on a filed external support line (an attestation, or a blind re-derivation that agrees, produced under C091-5's protocol). Re-examination of same-lineage material changes nothing. The program's independently supported count is at all times exactly 6 (M044, M047, M124, M202, M329, M330) plus the anchors with landed external lines; an anchor whose only producible support after the pass remains same-lineage stays internal-only and the count stands (register falsifier of GR-088-02).

falsifier: any of the 28 retaining a disposition sourced from the historical battery after the corrected run is filed; a corrected-run disposition not reflected in the anchor records; or a re-run executed under the historical battery or an unversioned variant of it.
statement: The corrected battery is run over the 28 Phase-48 promotions standing at requires-revalidation (the WP5 Phase-48 subset), as a run under run-defs v1, cited by run id. Each promotion's disposition follows the run's recorded output; the historical battery's output is retired as evidence for all 28. If the re-run promotes a materially different set, the original promotions reclassify per the new run (register falsifier of GR-088-03 candidate 1).

falsifier: one of the 4 reclassified as supported on crosswalk-lineage material; or one left recorded as merely pending after a documented sourcing attempt found no outside attestation.
statement: M087, M165, M264, M311 (rule R5d, each resting solely on a crosswalk or literature import) receive a documented sourcing attempt for an independent support line outside the crosswalk lineage (an owner act for the external engagement, D-091-1). Where an outside line lands, the disposition follows it; where no source outside the crosswalk lineage attests the readings, the 4 stay requires-revalidation permanently, recorded as structural rather than pending (register falsifier of GR-088-03 candidate 3).

falsifier: a byte change in any frozen record attributable to this spec; or a disposition change in audit v2 with no corresponding recorded act and named generator inputs.
statement: All status changes this spec produces (W1's eligibility classes, W2's support classes, W3's revalidation dispositions) land as recorded reclassification acts and in a new versioned anchor-support audit (audit v2, decision D-091-3) whose generator and inputs are named. The WP5 audit JSON, the WP4 provenance JSON, the historical Phase-48 battery and its output, and the original crosswalk file are never edited by any stage.

falsifier: one of the 5 whose post-revalidation disposition is not its corrected checker's recorded output; or one restored to a supported class without a new support line on record.
statement: M042, M046, M108 (rule R5b) and M176, M342 (rule R5c) are revalidated with the repair brief's corrected checkers over every arm that can run without GR-088-04's certification (the site-statistics lineage, site_stats_v2). Each anchor's disposition follows its checker's recorded output; where the v2 checkers judge the support insufficient, the anchors move to insufficient evidence, not back to supported (register falsifier of GR-088-03 candidate 2).

falsifier: a phonotactic violation count stated for any anchor under the uncertified rule set; or one of the 5 reclassified on a phonotactic basis before certification; or one of the 5 left at requires-revalidation after the site-statistics arm ran, without the GR-088-04 dependency named where the phonotactic arm was required.
statement: For any of the 5 single-line anchors whose revalidation requires the phonotactic checker (phonotactics_v2), that arm waits for GR-088-04's linguist-certified rule set. Until it lands, the affected anchors remain at requires-revalidation with the GR-088-04 dependency named on their records; no phonotactic violation count, in either direction, is produced for any anchor under the uncertified rule set. GR-088-04 is a separate register entry: this spec notes the dependency and does not absorb the linguist leg.

falsifier: a corrected-battery run awarding credit for an absent input, an unexecuted check, or a default branch, whether found in the battery's code or in a run record; or an enumerated historical pass-by-default path with no fixture proving its corrected behavior.
statement: In the corrected Phase-48 battery (a new versioned battery, decision D-091-4; the historical phase48_medium_validation.py is frozen), every promotion credit is earned by an executed check over present inputs. A missing input, an unexecuted check, or an inapplicable test produces not-run or fail, never credit. The removed pass-by-default paths are enumerated against the historical battery and the WP5 reconstruction, and each enumerated path has a fixture proving it now yields not-run/fail.

falsifier: one of the 46 with no recorded outcome; an attempt by a reader inside the anchor's derivation lineage; or an outcome recorded with no protocol on record.
statement: The outside-reproduction pass covers all 46 anchors of the WP5 audit's supported_internal_only class, under a protocol recorded before the pass starts: for each anchor, independent attestation or blind re-derivation by readers who did not produce the original derivations (decision D-091-1). Each anchor's outcome is recorded (external line landed, attempted and not landed, or not attempted with the reason), and the census is 46 accounted of 46.

falsifier: a component of P, or a step of its invariance argument, that cites a physics result, a bookkeeping quantity, or a recorded profile as its ground; or a component whose value over a fixed table can change without the table changing.
statement: The separator of this stage (the identity-structure profile P and its comparison) is defined using only the frozen G1 document v1.1's terms (the candidate state, the projection π and its sequence table T, projection-equivalence under §2.3, the exercised inventory) and the skeleton's D5 form. No physics result, no register or ledger quantity, and no quantity defined against a recorded corpus's profile is a component or a premise of the definition. This does not establish: that P is a good separator — only that its definition stands on the G1 document's terms, as D-090-3 requires of everything this study derives.

falsifier: a CISI scan, or any restricted source material, present in the stage's records or outputs; or a stage output that redistributes restricted content rather than statistics computed from records the repository already holds openly.
statement: The held-out set contains no CISI scans and no restricted material of any class; H1 enters the stage's records as statistics and computed profiles only. CISI-derived material plays no part in this stage's design (the `mayig-cisi` subset is excluded at §3.3), and nothing restricted is copied into the repository by any stage act. This does not establish: anything about the CISI restriction itself — only that this stage's design never needs to touch it.

falsifier: a ledger diff attributable to a G3 stage PR beyond the adoption append's lines; or an Indus claim reclassified, annotated, or re-scored citing this stage.
statement: Across the whole G3 stage, the claims ledger's diff is exactly the append of this stage's claim bundle (C090-17..24) through the sanctioned intake at adoption, plus the generated-layer regeneration that append forces. No stage act adjudicates, reclassifies, annotates, or scores any claim; no claim about the Indus script changes status, stage, or score; the program's standing position (the Indus script is not deciphered) is untouched, and nothing in this stage is a decipherment claim or evidence for one. This does not establish: anything about the appended claims' truth — only that the ledger's one-way flow survives the stage intact (C090-13's boundary, renewed).

falsifier: a profile, spectrum, or exploratory computation over H1 dated before the freeze record's commit; or a frozen item changed with no amendment act recorded.
statement: A freeze record carrying the items §3.4 enumerates is committed before the first profile over H1 is computed by anyone, for any purpose including exploration. Post-freeze changes are recorded amendment acts; an amendment touching the case list, the profile definitions, or the bar voids the administration. This does not establish: that the frozen design is wise — only that it was fixed before it met the data, which is what makes the administration a test rather than a fit.

falsifier: an outcome record whose SEPARATED rests on a component, case, or threshold absent from the freeze; or a re-run under this package following a recorded miss.
statement: The stage outcome is adjudged exactly by §5's three conditions over the frozen case list and the frozen profile definitions. No component is added, dropped, or re-weighted after any profile is seen; no case is substituted; no second administration under this package repairs a miss. A miss is recorded as NOT YET or CANNOT BE ADMINISTERED, with the obstruction named. This does not establish: that §5's bar is the only fair bar — only that it is the one this stage froze and answered to.

falsifier: the stage closing with no outcome record; an outcome stated in vocabulary the skeleton does not define without mapping to its terms; a SEPARATED reported to the registry in stronger words than the outcome record's own; or no report delivered after the outcome record lands.
statement: The stage closes with an outcome record stating the G3 outcome (SEPARATED, NOT YET with the obstruction named, or CANNOT BE ADMINISTERED with the forcing counts shown), the audited profiles, and the study-level outcome in the study's vocabulary (INSTANTIATES-path at most; ANALOGY if §6's pressure is the honest reading, with the element named). The outcome is reported to the VEXA chat for the improvement registry as a stage deliverable. The formal verdict over the full G1–G5 bar belongs to the independent reader under the judging protocol; this stage does not issue it. This does not establish: that the reported outcome is the final verdict on the domain — the reader's verdict, and G4/G5, stand after it.

falsifier: a G1/G2-era record, or a record they cite as computed grounding, that contains a table, profile, or per-record computation over H1; or an extraction rule in the freeze that selects records by any property a G1/G2 computation produced.
statement: No step of the G1 drafting, the adversarial pass, the G2 derivation, or the G2 audit computed a table, a profile, or a per-record quantity over H1 (the snapshot's `indusscript-m77` text-code records). The uses that exist are named and bounded: G1 §1.5's file-level census lines about the snapshot as a whole. The freeze record states the extraction rules, the permitted freeze counts, and the H1↔M77-flat-file object overlap it measured. This does not establish: that H1's objects are disjoint from the design corpora's — the claim is about computation, and the overlap number is published with the freeze so its weight is the reader's to judge.

falsifier: an audited control profile differing from A0's in any component, with the administration nevertheless reported as meeting the bar.
statement: For the frozen controls (the seeded relabeling C1; the identity C2), the audited profiles equal A0's in every component. A control that separates refutes the separator as implemented (and, if the implementation is faithful, as defined) under D5's invariance clause, and the stage records that as its finding. This does not establish: invariance for arbitrary equivalences beyond the controls — the controls are the test the bar sets; the general invariance is §2's arithmetic, which the controls sample at its most failure-prone point (a full relabeling).

falsifier: a diff in this spec's stages that moves a claim status, alters the token file's handling, touches edge secret handling, or changes a UI surface's behaviour.
statement: No claim's status, stage, or score moves under this spec; no settling verdict is re-adjudicated; the Spec 082 install-token file is untouched (a bearer credential by design — password audit §6, a different custody class, listed and not graded there); the cloud edge's secret custody (Worker secrets, D1 hashes) is untouched; no wireframe-gated UI surface changes (the settings surface's behaviour is contract-identical under C092-5). This does not establish: that the out-of-scope surfaces are sound — only that they are out of this spec's scope, each with its own record.

falsifier: a teardown ERROR of that family on any suite run after the fix lands; or a discharge claimed on fewer than the five named runs, or on runs not named.
statement: The mechanism behind suite divergence shape #1 (run-defs v1 §5: teardown ERROR entries of the sqlite closed-database family on tray test ids, first instance `test_tray_token_auth.py::test_copy_api_token_without_tkinter_is_named`) is identified in the stage record with its evidence, and the defect is fixed at its source in the fixture/connection lifecycle. Discharge requires five consecutive full-suite runs, named by run id (CI runs or bound local light records), with zero teardown ERRORs on tray tests; on discharge the shape's run-defs registration is amended by act (D-092-3) to record the fix, so a recurrence is a new unexplained junction, not a known shape to rerun away. This does not establish: that no other teardown flake exists — only that this family's mechanism is found, fixed, and watched by a stated bar.

falsifier: a local full-suite enumeration after this stage that stalls on the test, or deselects it by an unregistered manual act; or a stall explanation asserted in the record without profile evidence.
statement: A stage record states where the stall's time goes, from profile evidence gathered on this VM, for `test_phase392_q2_gate.py::test_pipeline_deterministic_under_seed` (which stalls for tens of minutes locally, equally on pristine `origin/main` — environmental in shape, unexplained in fact). The local path then takes exactly one of the two registered outcomes: the test completes within a stated budget on the VM, or its deselection becomes a named, environment-scoped registration (run-defs entry or the suite-runner configuration of record) with the CI backend job as its authoritative runner. No later enumeration depends on an operator remembering to deselect it by hand. This does not establish: that the test becomes fast, or that its determinism assertion may be weakened — D-092-4 forbids buying the budget by weakening what the test asserts.

falsifier: a full-suite run after this stage whose post-run `git status` under a watched root is non-empty absent a recorded disposition for that run, or whose suite light record shows a guard-skipped test.
statement: Spec 089 S4 made in-tree rewrites visible (the rewrite manifest over the watched roots `glossa-indus/claims/`, `glossa-indus/reports/`) and dispositioned; this claim closes the remainder: after a full-suite run, `git status` under the watched roots and the repo-root `outputs/` path is empty with no restore step — tests that regenerate artifacts write to isolated copies, or the regeneration is the test's own asserted output in a temp tree. The manifest remains as the detection instrument, but restoration stops being a routine post-run act, and the count of run-scoped tests skipped by the clean-tree precondition guard in a full-suite run is zero (S2's enumeration skipped 8 of 13 that way; the guard, not the tests, is what retires). This does not establish: that tests never write files — only that they never write the live tree they are measuring.

falsifier: a seeded class that escapes the battery as an untyped error, lands silently, or is exercised only on a developer machine and not in CI.
statement: The fault-injection battery modelled on the safe-write self-test (14 checks there) runs in the repo's CI: permission-denied writes, silent 0-byte landings, short writes, and missing or non-directory parents each surface as the typed error with the target preserved. The construction production runs is the construction the battery exercises, on the CI runners as well as locally. This does not establish: that real write-denial waves behave exactly like the seeds — the classes are the observed ones, and the claim covers exactly those.

falsifier: take the `.keys.json` from a configured install, with full knowledge of the format and the code, but without the key material, and recover any one stored credential value from the file bytes alone (substring search over the raw bytes, JSON parse, encoding-decode of every field).
statement: Every credential-class value the settings store persists — the provider API keys, the SMTP password, and the long-lived Microsoft Graph refresh token (`ms_graph_refresh_token`), per the credential set the stage registers — is encrypted under an authenticated-encryption construction with a fresh random nonce per value before it is written. The store file's bytes contain no stored credential value: not as a JSON string, not base64- or hex-encoded, not as any contiguous substring. This does not establish: protection against an adversary who executes code as the same OS user on the live host — the store must be decryptable by the backend process, and that boundary is named, not hidden (the threat this claim closes is the audit's: a reader of the data dir — a copy, a snapshot, a backup, another user — holding the file but not the key).

falsifier: a copy of `{data_dir}` alone — the snapshot/migration shape — suffices to decrypt a stored value; or key bytes found anywhere under `{data_dir}` or in the repo tree.
statement: The key is loaded from the custody location decision D-092-1 selects, which is outside `{data_dir}`. No copy of the key material is written into `{data_dir}`, into the repository, or into any artifact the data dir's own copy path carries (the Spec 080 snapshot and migration shape: this program copies its whole data dir, and a key inside it would travel with every copy). This does not establish: protection against an operator who deliberately exports both the data dir and the key — only that the program's own copy paths never bundle them.

falsifier: a caller of the helper observes a reported success whose on-disk bytes differ from the content written; or a write-path failure (a denied write, a missing or non-directory parent) escaping the helper as an untyped exception; or an empty write landing through it.
statement: `backend/glossa_lab/` gains a supported module implementing the safe-write contract the fleet's tooling (`~/workspace/system/safe-write/`) already proves: temp file in the target's own directory, fsync, atomic rename, read-back hash verification, a bounded retry ladder that includes a fresh-subprocess attempt (write denial is sticky per process lineage), refusal of empty content, parents never created implicitly, and a typed error — never a bare `OSError` — when every path fails. The module is the documented way repo code writes state that matters; the keys store is its first adopter of record. This does not establish: durability against a storage stack that lies below fsync — the contract is verification against read-back, which is the failure class the fleet actually met (denied writes and silent 0-byte landings), named as such.

falsifier: a diff in any consumer module required by the stage; or a behavioural difference in the masked status surface or `get_key` results over a fixture store, before versus after the stage, for the same inputs.
statement: `get_key`'s resolution order (process env over stored), the placeholder filtering, the masked GET status shape, the PUT semantics (including the process-env side effect), and every consumer — the settings API, `notifications/smtp.py`, `notifications/graph.py`, the notifications API's Graph save/disconnect path, the discovery and study-loop schedulers, and the database init's prefs migration — behave identically to the pre-stage code. All access continues to funnel through `api/settings.py`'s store functions; no consumer gains a direct file read. This does not establish: that the consumers are themselves secure — only that this stage does not move their contract while it changes the storage form underneath them.

falsifier: under fault injection — write denied at open, write landing 0 bytes, rename-time failure — the target's bytes after the failed call differ from its bytes before it, on either the helper path or the keys-store path.
statement: Because a verified write lands by renaming a fully written temp file, any failure before the rename leaves the prior target byte-identical. The keys store's save path writes through this construction from Stage 1 (retiring the direct `write_text`, whose truncating open can destroy the only copy of every stored credential before a denied write lands — the write-denial evidence of 2026-10-30), and its library form from Stage 2. This does not establish: protection against deletion or corruption of the file by means outside the write path.

falsifier: a store-writing module in the tree that the census does not name, found by the gate or by audit.
statement: The writers Stage 1 and Stage 2 create or move (the encrypted store's save path, the verified-write module's adopters of record) are registered under the V9 writer-census discipline Spec 089 S5 established, so the census the gate computes finds exactly the registered set. The standing gate profile after this spec is whatever the gate's own output states on the final tree, recorded verbatim in the closeout. This does not establish: that unregistered writers are impossible — only that this spec's surface is fully inside the census the gate runs.

falsifier: a legacy fixture store whose post-migration `get_key` results differ from its pre-migration results for any key; or a migration failure (key absent, write denied) after which the original file's bytes changed.
statement: On the first load after the upgrade, a store in the legacy plaintext format is read, rewritten in the encrypted format through the verified-write construction (C092-7), and proven by re-reading: every value present before migration is returned identically by `get_key` after it, and the credential set encrypted is exactly the registered set. An absent or credential-free store is a no-op, not a migration. A failed migration leaves the original file byte-untouched and the failure named — there is no half-migrated state. This does not establish: migration of any particular live install — the desktop install's store is migrated when Stage 1 deploys there, and its proof is that stage's record against the live store's key census (names and counts, never values).

falsifier: the ERROR recurring after an UNREPRODUCED closure without the item reopening; or a closure asserted on less than the stated battery.
statement: `test_notifications_api.py::test_mask_email_redacts_local_part` carries one ERROR sighting (2026-11-01) and no classification. The stage runs a stated battery — 50 repetitions of the notifications module standalone plus 3 full-suite-order runs — and the item ends in exactly one state: reproduced, and then classified (a named flake family, or a defect fixed at its source under C092-9's pattern); or not reproduced anywhere in the battery, and closed UNREPRODUCED with the battery as the evidence of record. The closure record carries its own reopening term: a later sighting reopens the item automatically. This does not establish: that the test is correct — only that its error state no longer sits unclassified, which is the defect this item carries.

falsifier: replace or remove the key on a configured install and observe the settings API report the keys as simply unset, or observe any credential value served; or remove the key and observe the backend fail to start without a named store error in its log.
statement: When a store file exists but cannot be decrypted — missing key, wrong key, corrupt or tampered ciphertext — the settings surface reports a named error state that distinguishes it from "no keys configured," and no credential is served from it. The loader never falls back to parsing an encrypted store as plaintext, and never presents an undecryptable store as empty (the current loader's silent-`{}`-on-any-error behaviour is retired for the encrypted path). A startup-path reader that cannot tolerate the failure (the database init's one-time prefs migration) must skip with a logged reason, never crash the backend and never silently proceed as if unconfigured. This does not establish: availability — a lost key still loses the stored credentials, and re-entry is the recovery; the claim is that the loss is loud and named, never silent.
